The stomach keeps me for the food,
The battery needs me for its charge.
ciphers.hint: A chemical substance that reacts with bases and can burn or corrode.

poem_stanzas:
I am the element of life,
Four bonds to build a world of shapes;
I am the diamond and the coal,
The graphite in the pencil dark.

I am the base of every living thing,
I cycle through the air and soil;
My fourteen tells the age of bones,
And with two of oxygen I make the breath we give.
ciphers.hint: The chemical element that forms the basis of all known life.

poem_stanzas:
Within the throat a hollow bridge is strung,
Two folded cords that quiver when I speak,
I shelter breath before it becomes song,
And close to guard the road that food must take.

When a cold descends, my gates grow rough and sore,
A whisper cracks where once a trumpet rang,
I am the singer's hidden, hinged door,
The reed the air must pass to find a name.
ciphers.hint: The voice box perched at the top of the windpipe.

poem_stanzas:
Deep in the hardest chambers I reside,
A soft and fatty treasure none can see,
I brew the blood that floods the body's tide,
And nurse the cells that make a remedy.

An oxtail stew once coaxed me to the spoon,
A proverb says I reach down to the bone,
In winter I am warmth, and hunger soon
Will crack me from my cage to feed its own.
ciphers.hint: The soft core hidden inside your largest bones.

poem_stanzas:
I am a quiet workshop small and sealed,
That drips a potent drop into the blood,
No pipe of mine is seen, no door revealed,
Yet messages I send like hidden flood.

Some of me weep upon the skin in heat,
Some sit beneath the jaw and swell with ill,
I answer signals with a silent beat,
A chemical whisper bent to body's will.
ciphers.hint: A tiny organ that pours out hormones or sweat.

poem_stanzas:
Two sisters of a cord share one broad band,
They ride the upper limb and pull it in,
When I am flexed you see a rounded land,
A knot of power that protects from sin.

Heaving and hoisting loads is my employ,
The boxer's coiled spring, the rower's friend,
I shorten, and the forearm swings with joy,
Then lengthen slow to let the labor end.
ciphers.hint: The two-headed muscle you flex to show strength.

poem_stanzas:
A cradle made of bone, a bowl, a ring,
That carries soft and heavy things above,
Two wings that meet and hold the weight of spring,
A gate through which new life must learn to move.

Among the skeleton I am the floor,
The lower ribs descend to find my rim,
I bear the trunk and steady it the more,
And cup the organs at the body's brim.
ciphers.hint: The basin of bone that holds the lower organs.

poem_stanzas:
Between the knee and ankle I stand guard,
The bone that fronts the leg and takes the blow,
I wear no muscle where the skin is hard,
And sting for days when tables catch me low.

I am the part you rub when you have tripped,
The striker's bruise, the child's first scrape and tear,
Down to the foot my slender length is slipped,
The bare and bony edge that stands so near.
ciphers.hint: The front of the lower leg, easy to bark.

poem_stanzas:
I face the ground and never see the sky,
I bear your weight and print a shape in sand,
With every step I flatten, then I rise,
The lowest floor of any standing land.

A cobbler works on me with thread and awl,
I thin where heels grind hardest on the street,
I hold a pebble like a bitter ball,
The tender map of everywhere you meet.
ciphers.hint: The flat underside of your foot.

poem_stanzas:
Above the skull a living carpet grows,
That sheds and bristles, pale or dark or grey,
The barber tends me where the crown wind blows,
And hats and helmets rest on me all day.

I prickle when a whisper names a fright,
I blush beneath the sun and burn to red,
I am the first to silver into white,
The stretch that holds the forest on your head.
ciphers.hint: The skin and hair covering the top of your head.

poem_stanzas:
I am long and lean and made to enter holes,
A musky hunter with a pointed face,
My coat is cream, my nose is black, and all
My joy is threading tunnels I can trace.

A hunter once would send me down a burrow,
I flush the frightened creature from its den,
Domestic now, I coil and sleep and borrow
The sleeves and drawers and human hands again.
ciphers.hint: A slim, fierce hunter once used to chase rabbits.

poem_stanzas:
Upon one island only do I swing,
A ring-tailed climber with a fox's face,
My eyes are round and bright, my fingers cling,
I leap the forest with a ghostly grace.

I bask with arms thrown wide to catch the sun,
My scent is musk, my call a wailing cry,
When night descends my waking has begun,
A stranger swinging through a southern sky.
ciphers.hint: A wide-eyed primate with a long tail, found only on one island.

poem_stanzas:
A forest cat with tassels on my ears,
A stub for tail, a coat of dappled grey,
I pad on silent feet through snowy years,
And see the hare before it turns to flee.

My eyes are wide and amber in the dark,
My beard hangs long and white beneath my chin,
The northern wood is where I leave my mark,
A tufted, silent hunter, lean and thin.
ciphers.hint: A wild cat with tufted ears and a very short tail.

poem_stanzas:
A tawny ghost that haunts the western hills,
A lion's cousin with an unknown name,
I leap the canyon where the cold air spills,
And stalk the deer with neither sound nor flame.

Alone I range, a shadow in the scrub,
No pride to keep me company at night,
I claim a ridge and hunt and sleep and rub
My flanks on bark to mark my hard-won right.
ciphers.hint: A large tawny cat also called a cougar or mountain lion.

poem_stanzas:
Upon a ceiling I can walk at ease,
My padded toes grip glass and plaster wall,
I drop my tail to buy my life when seized,
And it returns, though shorter after all.

My eyes are huge and lidless, always wet,
I chirp a little answer in the night,
A household friend for those who do not fret,
I chase the mosquito in the lamp's warm light.
ciphers.hint: A small lizard that climbs smooth walls with sticky toes.

poem_stanzas:
A spiny dragon of the tropics, I
Bask on a branch and wear a crest of scales,
My dewlap hangs, my whip-like tail can fly,
And green as leaves I hide from searching eyes.

When danger comes I dive into the stream,
A swimmer when I must, though born to climb,
I eat the flowers of the forest's dream,
And grow from small to armored over time.
ciphers.hint: A big crested lizard that lives in tropical treetops.

poem_stanzas:
We live in towns beneath the dusty sand,
And one of us must always stand and stare,
Upright on hind legs like a tiny man,
To watch the sky for wings that hunt from air.

If hawks appear, a whistle starts the rush,
We pour into the tunnels of our home,
Sunbathing in a huddle, warm and lush,
When cold mornings the desert turn to stone.
ciphers.hint: A small burrowing mammal that stands sentinel in the desert.

poem_stanzas:
Nocturnal, stout, and built down near the ground,
I dig a den with front teeth like a spade,
My pouch faces backward so no dirt is found
Within, and all my tunnels I have made.

Among the gum trees of the south I roam,
My droppings come out cubed and neat and square,
A slow and stubborn master of my home,
With powerful claws and coarse and dusty hair.
ciphers.hint: A stocky Australian digger that leaves cube-shaped droppings.

poem_stanzas:
A plump and speckled wanderer of fields,
I run on foot and seldom take to wing,
My body crouched, my feathers are my shields,
I bob and whistle when the mornings sing.

A covey of my kin will rise at once,
Exploding from the stubble in a blur,
We scatter, then regroup among the stems,
And fold again as quiet as we were.
ciphers.hint: A small plump ground bird that bobs its head as it walks.

poem_stanzas:
A little singer of the garden hedge,
My beak is thick to crack the hardest seed,
I flit in yellow, red, or brown, and edge
The feeder where the other birds will feed.

My trills are short and cheerful in the thorn,
I build a cup of grass and moss and hair,
And when the winter strips the field of corn,
I find a feeder hung in city air.
ciphers.hint: A small seed-eating songbird with a stout beak.

poem_stanzas:
I rise on quivering wings above the field,
And sing the higher that I climb the blue,
A speck of morning, hidden and revealed,
A shower of music falling down to you.

To wake before the sun and mount the sky,
To pour a fountain from a burning throat,
Is joy enough; I need no reason why,
I am the morning's own ascending note.
ciphers.hint: A brown bird famous for singing while soaring high.

poem_stanzas:
Upon a chimney I have built my nest,
On legs like stilts I wade the shallow mere,
With clapping bill I greet my mate and rest,
And fly on wings that carry far and clear.

A legend says I bring the newborn down,
A bundle dangling from a crimson beak,
I stand in fields of frogs beyond the town,
And winter drives me south for months to seek.
ciphers.hint: A tall long-legged bird said to deliver babies.

poem_stanzas:
A grey and stately dancer of the marsh,
I bugle with a trumpet in my throat,
On folded wings I rise, and winters harsh
I flee on high for warmer lands remote.

On one leg I may stand the whole night through,
My courtship is a leaping, bowing dance,
A folded bird in paper, inked and true,
That hangs above a sickroom's quiet glance.
ciphers.hint: A tall stately bird that dances and trumpets its call.

poem_stanzas:
Upon the water I am a floating boat,
My bill a basket scooped to hold the sea,
I drain the brine and swallow what will float,
And share the catch with nestlings under me.

On posts and piers I stand with folded wings,
A pale and solemn sentinel of shore,
My hanging pouch is full when fishing brings
A crowd of silver wriggling in its store.
ciphers.hint: A big waterbird with a huge throat pouch for scooping fish.

poem_stanzas:
Upon one slender leg I stand and wade,
My curving neck descends in shallows gray,
The brine I sieve has dyed me where I feed,
And turned my feathers into flushed display.

In crowds of thousands I am seen to dance,
I bow and flag my wings to win a mate,
My courtship is a ballet at a glance,
And colonies of rose await my fate.
ciphers.hint: A wading bird that stands on one leg and turns pink from its food.

poem_stanzas:
I bear a bill too huge to seem my own,
A painted blade of orange, black and gold,
It stretches past my eye, a boastful bone,
And sifts the jungle fruit my branches hold.

My forest rings with croaks and clacks and trills,
I nest within a hollow in a tree,
A flash of color in the wooded hills,
A bird the size of mischief, bold and free.
ciphers.hint: A tropical bird with an enormous colorful bill.

poem_stanzas:
I cling to branches with a grip of two,
And nap for hours while the sun is high,
My diet is a gum-leaf, tough to chew,
Across the treetops I am slow to fly.

My nose is broad and black, my coat is grey,
My pouch is slung to hold my baby near,
I climb where fragrant branches bend and sway,
And munch a bitter leaf through all the year.
ciphers.hint: A sleepy Australian tree-dweller that eats eucalyptus leaves.

poem_stanzas:
I hang beneath a branch with hooking claws,
And move so slowly moss will grow on fur,
For weeks I drowse and break no forest laws,
And rarely hurry, rarely even stir.

I climb down only when I need to go,
A single errand, then I climb again,
My motions are a minute, soft and slow,
And patience is the measure of my den.
ciphers.hint: A slow tree-hanging mammal of the American tropics.

poem_stanzas:
A shaggy ox upon the roof of earth,
My skirt of hair hangs low against the cold,
My horns are curved, my lungs are wide for air,
I chew the mossy grass on mountains old.

Herdsmen will comb my fleece to spin a rope,
And load me as a beast of burden, slow,
I carry milk and butter, fuel and hope,
Across the passes buried deep in snow.
ciphers.hint: A shaggy highland ox of the Himalayas.

poem_stanzas:
I climb the cliffs that others dare not try,
My hooves are pads that grip a ledge of stone,
My horns sweep backward, long and ridged and high,
And winter snows I face and face alone.

The hunter comes to claim my curving crown,
I leap from rock to rock and slip away,
The highest crags are where my kind look down,
The masters of the mountain and the day.
ciphers.hint: A wild mountain goat with long, ridged, backward-curving horns.

poem_stanzas:
A pebble thrown across the dark alone,
A grain of stone that wanders without aim,
I circle with the planets, cold as bone,
Until at last I find the earth's hot flame.

When I descend, my skin begins to glow,
The air will file me down to dust and hiss,
My trail becomes a wishing line below,
A falling star, a momentary kiss.
ciphers.hint: A small rocky body drifting through space before it burns.

poem_stanzas:
A bulging shape that hangs between two states,
Too fat for half, too lean to be a whole,
It swells and ripens while the evening waits,
A lopsided lantern for the owl and vole.

Two nights of this, then it will fill and smile,
Then shrink again through every darkening part,
The sky records each phase and files each mile,
A crescent, then a sliver, then no heart.
ciphers.hint: Describing a moon that is more than half but not fully round.

poem_stanzas:
After the brimming cup has overflowed,
I am the slow retreat, the shrinking edge,
Each evening takes a portion from the road,
Until I hang a lamp on a bent ledge.

I fade toward dark and vanish into none,
A single night of nothing, black and deep,
Then I return the other way, begun
Again to grow while all the world's asleep.
ciphers.hint: The moon's slow shrinking after it has been full.

poem_stanzas:
I am the farthest mark upon a loop,
The widest breath a satellite can draw,
The distant edge where it can slightly droop,
The loneliest point in a celestial law.

Across the ring there waits a closer twin,
Where orbit rushes and the pull is deep,
But I am where the circling slows, and in
That hush the moon and tide may go to sleep.
ciphers.hint: The point in an orbit farthest from the body it circles.

poem_stanzas:
I am the closest brush of any round,
Where circling speed is quickest and most near,
The tightest turn that any moon has wound,
The point where tides on earth begin to rear.

Across the way my distant brother waits,
Where every motion dawdles and is slow,
We are the two extremes of circling fates,
The near and far of every heavenly go.
ciphers.hint: The point in an orbit nearest the body it circles.

poem_stanzas:
Upon the burning face a blemish grows,
A darker island than the blazing sea,
It rises and departs and comes and goes
In cycles that astronomers can see.

I weigh a hundred earths and still I hide
Within the glare that blinds the unaided eye,
I fling a banner down the solar tide,
And paint the polar night with fire on high.
ciphers.hint: A cooler dark patch on the surface of the sun.

poem_stanzas:
A halo of pale fire, a silver mane,
That only shows when day has been undone,
When the black disc devours the shining plain,
And all the birds have fallen silent, stunned.

I reach a million miles into the cold,
A streamer flung from an imprisoned light,
I am the sun's disheveled hair of gold,
That lingers when the sky is torn from night.
ciphers.hint: The pearly outer glow around the sun, seen at an eclipse.

poem_stanzas:
When two great bodies find themselves aligned,
I am the inmost blackness they create,
The cone of purest dark, the deepest blind,
Where light is utterly refused at the gate.

Beside me wanders a paler, looser shade,
A half-lit cousin at the shadow's rim,
I am the core where every sunbeam fled,
The perfect dark at evening's sudden brim.
ciphers.hint: The darkest, central part of a shadow during an eclipse.

poem_stanzas:
I am a tender ache that is not mine,
That blooms when someone else is bowed by pain,
I bring no remedy to lend or sign,
But I will sit beside you in the rain.

I am the sigh before the helping hand,
The knot that tightens at another's fall,
I am the bridge by which the lonely stand,
And mercy is the road I build for all.
ciphers.hint: The tender ache you feel for someone else's suffering.

poem_stanzas:
I come too late, a guest who will not leave,
When deeds are done and cannot be undone,
I sting the memory and make it grieve,
And turn the daylight grey beneath the sun.

I am the conscience with a burning coal,
The echo of a choice no plea can still,
I lodge forever in the guilty soul,
And no forgetting ever breaks my will.
ciphers.hint: The bitter regret for a wrong you have done.

poem_stanzas:
I am the hush before a mountain range,
The widening of the eye beneath the stars,
I make the smallness of a person plain,
And lift the heart above its daily bars.

I come with thunder and with ocean swells,
With newborn life and with the temple's dome,
I am the reverence that silence tells,
The trembling that makes every watcher home.
ciphers.hint: The feeling of wonder and reverence before something vast.

poem_stanzas:
I am the sour seed of small revenge,
That sprouts in one who feels they were denied,
I make a gentle heart turn hard and strange,
And find a bitter pleasure in the pride.

I am the reason pettiness survives,
The pinch of mean delight in another's loss,
I feed on slights and keep the grudge alive,
And nail my grievance to a polished cross.
ciphers.hint: A petty wish to wound or annoy out of resentment.

poem_stanzas:
I am a heavy shadow on the mind,
A grey that gathers when the light has gone,
A mood that makes the kindest world unkind,
And leaves the lonely sitting still till dawn.

I fill the corners of a winter room,
I muffle laughter and I dull the song,
I settle like a mist, a kind of tomb,
And hold the weary quietly too long.
ciphers.hint: A heavy, dark mood or darkness itself.

poem_stanzas:
I am the bubbling that escapes the chest,
The crinkling at the corner of the eyes,
I come when friends and foolish stories best
Unfold, and no one bothers to be wise.

I am the music of a roaring room,
The stamping and the slapping of the knee,
I chase the heavy shadow and its doom,
And leave the heart as light as it can be.
ciphers.hint: Laughter and gladness that spill out in company.

poem_stanzas:
I am the cry beneath the singer's note,
The aching undertow of deep despair,
I am the sorrow that the lonely tote,
The weight of every unanswered prayer.

I am the shadow of a shattered thing,
The far side of a lamentation's sound,
I am the grief that loss and parting bring,
And where I settle, joy is rarely found.
ciphers.hint: Deep sorrow; great trouble.

poem_stanzas:
I am the fire that reason cannot cool,
The burning engine of a chosen cause,
I make a person overstep the rule,
And never stop for comfort or applause.

I am the convert's and the martyr's flame,
The heat that drives the runner through the pain,
The blazing passion that outlives the shame,
The ardor that will labor all in vain.
ciphers.hint: Eager, passionate enthusiasm for a cause.

poem_stanzas:
Beneath the cold and heavy soil I swell,
A bulb that wears a tuft of leafy green,
The farmer pulls me from my earthy cell,
And heaps me in the barn to be unseen.

I am the lantern carved on harvest night,
A root that feeds the cattle through the cold,
A humble harvest for the laborer's bite,
A treasure from the dark and humble mould.
ciphers.hint: A round root vegetable, purple and white, grown in cold fields.

poem_stanzas:
A crimson button buried in the rows,
I ripen quick and crisp and peppery,
My shoulder pokes above, and someone knows
To pull me young, before I grow too free.

On salads I am sliced in rosy rings,
A little pepper-flavored crunch of spring,
I come to tables with the fresh green things,
And make a plainest sandwich into king.
ciphers.hint: A small crunchy red root with a peppery bite.

poem_stanzas:
A cousin of the carrot, pale and cream,
I bide all winter in the frozen ground,
Cold makes me sweet, though sweetness was a dream,
And in the roasting pan I am found.

On Sunday tables next to beef I lie,
A homely root that many overlook,
The winter frost will sweeten me, and I
Am eaten from a well-worn country cook.
ciphers.hint: A pale sweet root, like a carrot but cream-colored.

poem_stanzas:
I am a fan of dark green crinkled leaves,
That shrink to a small spoonful when they stew,
A sailor's cartoon strength the world believes,
And farmers sow me when the winter's through.

For those who need green strength I am the spring,
A leafy iron for the blood and bone,
And children push me round the plate and sing
A song of protest in a mournful tone.
ciphers.hint: A dark leafy green that makes Popeye strong.

poem_stanzas:
I am a little forest on a stalk,
A green umbrella of a thousand trees,
I grow in cool and cloudy garden walk,
And shiver in the season's later breeze.

I was not loved by every child at first,
A green and bitter challenge on the plate,
But steam me tender, and the tide is reversed,
And even fussy eaters clean their slate.
ciphers.hint: A green vegetable shaped like a little tree.

poem_stanzas:
I come in green and long and slender form,
A summer squash that swells while you're away,
I hide beneath a giant leaf from storm,
And double size within a single day.

Exhausted gardeners will leave a pile
Of me upon a neighbor's porch and run,
I bake into a bread that makes them smile,
And still there will be more when day is done.
ciphers.hint: A long green summer squash that grows overnight.

poem_stanzas:
A tiny coin of earth, a flattened seed,
That swells in water and becomes a meal,
I feed the humble household in its need,
And make a hearty soup that poor men feel.

From ancient fields of Egypt and of Rome,
I travel in a sack to fill a pot,
My shape is like a lens inside the home,
And thickens winter soup when it is hot.
ciphers.hint: A tiny flat seed cooked in soups and stews.

poem_stanzas:
I am a golden smooth and spoonable cream,
That wobbles gently on a saucer's rim,
I crown a pudding in a yellow stream,
And sweeten holidays with eager vim.

On winter tables I am spooned for all,
A dust of nutmeg settles on my skin,
A gentle blanket after dinner's call,
A comfort that the sweetest spoons begin.
ciphers.hint: A soft, sweet yellow dessert made of milk and eggs.

poem_stanzas:
A slender bridge of earth between two seas,
So thin the ships must take the longer road,
Two continents are linked by such as these,
And armies cross where water nearly flowed.

A canal was carved through me to join two seas,
Two oceans met when diggers cut my clay,
A narrow neck that lets the ships go free,
And shortens half the voyages of the day.
ciphers.hint: A narrow strip of land connecting two larger landmasses.

poem_stanzas:
A narrow gash that running water scored,
With walls that climb on either side in shade,
A hidden cleft where only water roared,
A trench the patient river slowly made.

A line too small to locate on a chart,
A place where climbers scramble to descend,
I hold the runoff of a mountain's heart,
And down my throat the flash floods slowly bend.
ciphers.hint: A deep, narrow gorge worn by running water.

poem_stanzas:
A purple waste of heather, wide and bare,
Where mist descends and lonely curlews cry,
A land of broken stone and open air,
Where only hardy sheep and grouse can lie.

Romances set their brooding dramas here,
A treacherous bog can swallow up a path,
I am the wind and emptiness and fear,
And all the lonely beauty aftermath.
ciphers.hint: An open, rough, poorly drained upland of heather and grass.

poem_stanzas:
I am an open stretch of purple bloom,
Where no tall tree will stand upon the soil,
A sandy, sunlit, bee-loud kind of room,
Where heather roots and windswept grasses coil.

The adder and the deer both share my land,
A common and a golf course bear my name,
The hiker crosses with a map in hand,
And here a fictional villain staked a claim.
ciphers.hint: An open area of low shrubs, especially heather.

poem_stanzas:
A rounded hump upon a gentle plain,
A little swell the glacier left behind,
A place to sit and watch the clouds and rain,
And let the long grass whistle in the wind.

A word of Old and Middle English birth,
A gentle rise is all my modest plea,
A grassy bump upon the tumps of earth,
A place where sheep can stand and watch the sea.
ciphers.hint: A small, low, rounded hill.

poem_stanzas:
I am a rounded heap of earth or stone,
A little hill on flat or marshy ground,
The pitcher's rubber rests on me alone,
And buried kings beneath me may be found.

An ant will raise me, and a mole will too,
A baseball pitcher stands upon my back,
A mountain is a giant version of me,
And ancient graves lie underneath my track.
ciphers.hint: A raised hill or heap, often of earth.

poem_stanzas:
A narrow spine of stone that splits the sky,
The line where two descending slopes have met,
A walker follows up and climbs so high,
And sees two valleys from my silhouette.

A plough will turn me in a field of loam,
A line of pressure on a weather chart,
I am the roof line of a mountain home,
And where the rains divide and part.
ciphers.hint: A long narrow raised crest of land or a mountain top line.

poem_stanzas:
A narrow arm the ocean sends ashore,
A finger of the tide that feels the land,
A sheltered cove where little waves explore,
And boats may hide from storms on either hand.

A bay is wider, and a fjord is steep,
I am the modest opening between,
A place where sheltered fishing boats may sleep,
A quiet cleft where land and sea convene.
ciphers.hint: A small arm of water reaching into the land.

poem_stanzas:
A slender pipe of dark and polished wood,
I speak through two thin reeds that pinch and sing,
An orchestra will tune to me for good,
And to my note the strings and horns will ring.

The duck's lament, the swan's soft final call,
The shepherd's voice in many a country score,
I am the pensive reed within the hall,
The plaintive note that opens childhood's door.
ciphers.hint: A slender double-reed woodwind with a plaintive tone.

poem_stanzas:
I am the deepest voice of any band,
A brass and coiling serpent on the knee,
I hold the bottom end with heavy hand,
And anchor all the march and melody.

My mouthpiece is the widest of the brass,
My notes are round and slow and seldom high,
Beneath the oompah beat I help it pass,
And carry all the bass that shakes the sky.
ciphers.hint: The largest, lowest brass instrument.

poem_stanzas:
A slender tube of high and piercing note,
I lead the marching column with my breath,
My cousin is the flute in a long coat,
And I have cheered a march to life from death.

A drum will keep me company in line,
A piccolo and I are close in blood,
I fit a palm and by a wrist design,
And cheer a village fair through rain and mud.
ciphers.hint: A small high-pitched flute used with drums in marching.

poem_stanzas:
A tortoise shell once served me as a frame,
Two curving horns with strings stretched in between,
The singer plucked me as he praised a name,
And music rose where mourning had just been.

Apollo taught its use to mortal hands,
It walked with poets down the classic years,
It stands for lyric verse in many lands,
And shares its shape with quiet, heavenly spheres.
ciphers.hint: An ancient stringed instrument played by poets.

poem_stanzas:
A piece in parts, a journey with three stops,
A first that states, a slow one that may sing,
A final that returns and turns and drops,
A conversation with no words to bring.

The classical composers shaped my form,
For keyboard or for violin or reed,
I am a little drama, quiet or storm,
A wordless argument that players read.
ciphers.hint: A multi-movement instrumental work, often for piano or solo.

poem_stanzas:
I am the settling of a wandering line,
The fall that tells the ear a phrase is through,
The comfortable close, the final sign,
The point where resolutions come in view.

A full one rests and seals the homeward key,
A half still hangs a question in the air,
A plagal one comes down so quietly,
And marching feet will find me everywhere.
ciphers.hint: The closing sequence of chords that ends a phrase.

poem_stanzas:
Above the waist a man, below a goat,
With pointed ears and horns and shaggy thighs,
I play a reedy pipe in woodland note,
And chase the fleeing nymph with greedy eyes.

I follow Dionysus in his train,
A wild and wine-soaked reveler at his side,
I am the forest's mischief and its bane,
And through me all the ancient wildwoods ride.
ciphers.hint: A woodland creature, half man and half goat.

poem_stanzas:
A horse with feathered pinions, born of blood,
Who sprang from where a severed neck had bled,
I strike a spring from stone in a green wood,
And carry heroes where no road is led.

A rider urged me up to slay a beast,
A poet rode me to the sacred hill,
I serve the thunder's master at his feast,
And must be caught with bridle and with will.
ciphers.hint: The winged horse of Greek myth.

poem_stanzas:
Upon a rock I sing a honeyed song,
That lures the sailor from his steady track,
My voice is sweet, my purpose is the wrong,
And ships have broken on my singing back.

One hero filled his sailors' ears with wax,
And bound himself to listen and to live,
He learned how close my honeyed music tracks,
And steered away from all I had to give.
ciphers.hint: A creature whose singing lured sailors to their doom.

poem_stanzas:
I live beneath a bridge or in a hill,
A grumpy, hulking giant of the north,
At night I hoard my gold and keep quite still,
By day I turn to stone and venture forth.

Three billy goats once crossed my bridge and won,
And I was thrown into the river's foam,
A child may find me in the tale of fun,
And in the comments of the internet home.
ciphers.hint: A cave-dwelling giant of northern folklore, or a bridge toll-keeper.

poem_stanzas:
A tiny spirit of the air and brook,
A playful flicker in the forest shade,
I dance on dew and vanish with a look,
And leave a ring of mushrooms where I played.

A pixel figure borrows my small name,
A lively thing that flits across a screen,
A fairy-ring and I are much the same,
And both are gone as soon as they are seen.
ciphers.hint: A small, mischievous fairy spirit.

poem_stanzas:
I live and die within a single tree,
My life is bound to bark and leaf and root,
When it is felled, I fade to memory,
And nothing of me leaves a branch or shoot.

An oak or olive is my only home,
A Greek once feared to fell a sacred grove,
I am the spirit of the wooded dome,
And with my tree I live and breathe and love.
ciphers.hint: A tree spirit of Greek myth.

poem_stanzas:
I am the softening after winter's freeze,
The dripping from the eaves at noon's first touch,
The loosening of rivers by degrees,
And mud that smells of spring and means so much.

A frozen pond becomes a sheet of slush,
A buried bulb will lift a weary head,
The garden wakes from its long frozen hush,
And every stream is finding its old bed.
ciphers.hint: The melting of snow and ice as warmth returns.

poem_stanzas:
I am a wind that has outgrown a breeze,
A roaring rush that bends the tallest oak,
I whip the waves and harry ships with ease,
And to a forest I am no kind joke.

A weather warning often bears my name,
A sailor watches for a lowering sky,
I am the punishment the winds became,
The fierce and roaring force that none deny.
ciphers.hint: A very strong wind.

poem_stanzas:
I am a sudden shove that comes and goes,
A single puff that snatches at your hat,
A little breath that lifts the dirt and blows,
And rattles every window where it sat.

A leaf will dance and then the air is still,
I come between the calms on blustery days,
A sail will fill and slacken on a hill,
And dust will settle after all my ways.
ciphers.hint: A sudden brief rush of wind.

poem_stanzas:
I am the rain that hardened on the way,
A rattling handful on the pane and roof,
A stinging grain that turns the pavement gray,
A brittle, bouncing, frozen kind of proof.

Beneath me roads become a skating rink,
I drum upon the windshield and the hood,
A winter blend that hovers on the brink
Of snow and rain, and neither, understood.
ciphers.hint: Frozen rain that falls as ice pellets.

poem_stanzas:
I am the sudden color of the year,
The petaled opening of a long wait,
The proof that all the growing time is here,
The beauty that the gardener cannot rate.

A rose will make a season of my name,
A cherry tree will bury streets in pink,
A gardener will coax me into flame,
And in a week I wither on the brink.
ciphers.hint: A flower, or the time a plant opens its flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A golden dust that rides upon the bee,
A grain of life that travels bloom to bloom,
A sneeze in spring for those who breathe in me,
A yellow coat that settles in a room.

A watery eye will redden at my drift,
The wind may carry me for miles and more,
I am the father of the orchard's gift,
The yellow promise at the flower's core.
ciphers.hint: The fine powder from flowers that fertilizes other flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A tiny green beginning from a bean,
That pushes up through soil to find the light,
A promise of the garden yet unseen,
The first green foot of many a summer's height.

On sandwiches and salads I am found,
The bean and Brussels are my leafy kin,
A child may grow me in a jar, around
A window sill, from seed that's kept within.
ciphers.hint: A tiny new shoot growing from a seed.

poem_stanzas:
I climb the wall and hold with tiny feet,
A dark green army scaling brick and stone,
I swallow fences where the gardens meet,
And make an old house feel less alone.

A college wall is famous for my spread,
A carol pairs my name with holly's red,
I cover ruins where the roof is dead,
And starve the wall that dares to be my bed.
ciphers.hint: A climbing evergreen vine that covers walls.

poem_stanzas:
I hold a flame inside a frame of tin,
A little window and a hoop of wire,
I light the road when all the dark is in,
And guide a walking figure through the mire.

A paper version floats on water's face,
A festival will launch me to the sky,
A red one swings above a doorway's space,
And hollow pumpkins borrow from my eye.
ciphers.hint: A portable light enclosed in a case with a handle.

poem_stanzas:
I am a vessel with a swinging ear,
That hangs upon a hook beside a well,
I carry water, sand, and paint, and beer,
And in a sandbox I am king as well.

A child upon the beach will fill me up,
A janitor will dip me with a mop,
I take the milk before the calf will sup,
And I have hit the bottom with a plop.
ciphers.hint: An open container with a handle, used to carry liquids.

poem_stanzas:
I am a weight upon a shaft of wood,
That drives a nail and shapes the glowing steel,
A blacksmith's partner, builder's livelihood,
The sudden bang that makes a finger feel.

A gavel in a courtroom is my kin,
A claw behind my head will pull the nail,
I drive the metal home and split the skin,
And ring the anvil with a steady flail.
ciphers.hint: A tool with a heavy head used to drive nails.

poem_stanzas:
A blade with a wooden handle for the hand,
A sculptor's partner when he strikes a block,
I carve the marble, working as was planned,
And knock the unwanted stone with steady knock.

With a mallet I am driven, never struck,
A carpenter will pair me with a plane,
I make the grooves where joints will turn and tuck,
And wake the shape that sleeps in wood and vein.
ciphers.hint: A tool with a sharp edge for carving wood or stone.

poem_stanzas:
I sit upon a stove and gather steam,
A spout that whistles when the water boils,
I am the kitchen's warm and homely dream,
That fills a winter morning with my toils.

When camping, I am hung above a fire,
I pour the tea and steam the windowpane,
I whistle when the water climbs the wire,
And call the household to the table again.
ciphers.hint: A metal pot with a spout for boiling water.

poem_stanzas:
A blade both short and sharp for close at hand,
With edge and point and hilt for gripping tight,
A weapon hidden in a cloak or band,
A sudden glint that wakes the dark of night.

A Roman in the forum felt my sting,
A hidden hand could end a sleep or throne,
The word for me is used to mean a thing
That cuts a friendship to the very bone.
ciphers.hint: A short pointed knife used as a weapon.

poem_stanzas:
I ride upon the shoulder or the back,
A tube of leather or of painted wood,
I hold the slender shafts that never lack,
And keep the archer's deadly arrows good.

The same small word can mean to shake with fear,
So archers carry me and tremble too,
A hunter's gear for hunting fallow deer,
A bundle full of feathered sticks in view.
ciphers.hint: A case slung on the back to hold an archer's arrows.

poem_stanzas:
I sit upon a horse and take the weight,
A padded perch of leather and of steel,
I make the rider comfortable and straight,
And ease the long day's muscle and its feel.

A cowboy straps me on and rides away,
A stirrup dangles down on either side,
A bike and truck have borrowed me today,
And all my purpose is to give a ride.
ciphers.hint: A leather seat strapped on a horse for a rider.

poem_stanzas:
I have no charge, I sit within the core,
Beside a positive companion, bound,
Without me many atoms are no more,
And isotopes are made where I am found.

I split a heavy nucleus in two,
And loosed a power the world has feared and used,
A star that turns to one of me will strew
A pulse of light that sky-watchers have mused.
ciphers.hint: A neutral particle found in the nucleus of an atom.

poem_stanzas:
I carry positive within the core,
The count of me decides what element,
I sit with a companion and explore
The metal's name and all its ornament.

A giant accelerator will speed me fast,
Two hydrogen are made to race and meet,
A collider has studied me at last,
And found a host of particles more fleet.
ciphers.hint: A positively charged particle in an atom's nucleus.

poem_stanzas:
I am the pressure in an unseen stream,
The shove that sets the electrons on their way,
I come from cells and lightning and from steam,
And I am what the transformer must obey.

A bolt of lightning carries me in full,
A household socket holds a steady share,
A multimeter will read my pull,
And bulbs will brighten by the strength I bear.
ciphers.hint: The electrical pressure that pushes current through a wire.

poem_stanzas:
A ring of wire that must not break or gap,
The journey of a current out and back,
A broken one will blow a fuse's trap,
And leave a room in unforeseen attack.

On tracks a driver makes me many laps,
A breaker opens when the current spikes,
A logic board is full of me and maps,
And every charge must travel where I like.
ciphers.hint: A complete loop through which electricity flows.

poem_stanzas:
I am a folded chain that acts as a key,
I fit a shape and hurry it along,
Without me, all the body's chemistry
Would slow to nothing and the cells grow wrong.

I dwell in stomach, laundry soap, and seed,
My name will often end in a set of sounds,
I speed a chemical with no need
Of heat, and life on me in part abounds.
ciphers.hint: A protein that speeds up chemical reactions in living things.

poem_stanzas:
I am the drift of everything toward mess,
The reason time has only one direction,
The reason heat will scatter and digress,
And nothing ever ends in true perfection.

A broken cup will never mend alone,
A tidy room will slowly fall apart,
A physicist will find me in the drone
Of every engine, every human heart.
ciphers.hint: A measure of disorder; the tendency toward decay.

poem_stanzas:
Upon a lawn of summer I am played,
A wooden mallet strikes a painted ball,
Through little hoops a crooked path is laid,
And everyone must wait and take their call.

A flamingo was the mallet in a dream,
A hedgehog served as ball in Wonderland,
A gentle summer game of distant aim,
That ends with tea and a congratulating hand.
ciphers.hint: A lawn game played by hitting balls through hoops with mallets.

poem_stanzas:
I face the stern and pull with back and arm,
A sliding seat goes forward and retreats,
A rhythm that a crew must keep from harm,
A steely stroke that every oarsman beats.

An eight will fly with one and eight and cox,
A river race is where my speed is shown,
Two blades will bite the water's glassy locks,
And leave a trail of arrow heads alone.
ciphers.hint: Pulling oars to propel a boat.

poem_stanzas:
A spear of metal balanced in the palm,
I fly across the field in a long arc,
A running throw that keeps the shoulder calm,
And lands a point beyond the farthest mark.

An ancient warrior carried me to war,
An athlete now will hurl me for a prize,
I spin and slice the air and then I score,
A single tip that heaven-reaching flies.
ciphers.hint: A spear thrown as far as possible for distance.

poem_stanzas:
A row of wooden frames across the track,
That must be cleared with neither touch nor fall,
A rhythm of a leap and landing back,
A test of speed and nerve above them all.

An athlete's stride is counted to my beat,
A horse will clear me in a jumping course,
A life is full of me on every street,
And few approach me without some remorse.
ciphers.hint: Barriers a runner must leap over in a race.

poem_stanzas:
A flat and heavy plate of stone or steel,
That spins from out a circle on the ground,
A thrower whirls and lets the weight reveal,
The farthest arc that any arm has found.

A famous statue holds me in his hand,
An ancient game of Greece still sends me far,
I whirl and sail and settle in the sand,
A flattened sun that leaves a dusty scar.
ciphers.hint: A heavy flat disc thrown for distance.

poem_stanzas:
A game of mud and muscle and an egg,
Where hands will throw and feet will punt and run,
A scrum of giants shoving leg to leg,
A try that ends with all the fever done.

A school once picked the ball up from the ground,
And made a game of running with the thing,
The ball is oval, brown, and leather-bound,
And every player wears a mouthguard ring.
ciphers.hint: A team game with an oval ball, carrying and tackling.

poem_stanzas:
The largest vessel of the beating pump,
An arch of muscle rising from the heart,
I carry crimson outward in a jump,
And branch to every limb and every part.

A Roman cook once named me for the air,
My wall is thick to bear the surging tide,
If I should tear, the surgeon must repair
The flood that rushes from the opened side.
ciphers.hint: The great artery that carries blood out of the heart.

poem_stanzas:
Deep at the back within a darkened room,
I spread a screen where images are cast,
I turn the light to signals in the gloom,
And send them where the brain can hold them fast.

A doctor looks at me to find disease,
My cells can tear and float and blur the view,
The camera's film is cousin to my ease,
I am the eye's last, sensitive review.
ciphers.hint: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.

poem_stanzas:
I am the window at the front of sight,
A watch-glass clear and curved and deeply set,
I bend the light before it takes its flight,
And no red blood of mine will ever wet.

A scratch from grit or branch can make me sore,
A surgeon may replace me with a gift,
And when I cloud, the world grows dim and poor,
I am the pane that helps the vision lift.
ciphers.hint: The clear front surface of the eye.

poem_stanzas:
A colored ring around a darkling hole,
I widen when the night has come to stay,
I narrow when the sunlight takes its toll,
And guard the chamber where the pictures play.

My shades are blue and green and hazel, brown,
A flower of the same name is my twin,
I am the shutter of the eye's small town,
That opens wide or draws its curtain in.
ciphers.hint: The colored ring that controls the pupil's size.

poem_stanzas:
A rounded section of a larger whole,
A panel in the lung or in the brain,
I have my work assigned and keep my role,
And separate from my neighbors, not in vain.

An ear has one that dangles at its rim,
A lung is split in two, a brain in four,
The mind is mapped in regions, each a limb
Of thought, and each performs a separate chore.
ciphers.hint: A rounded division of an organ such as the brain or lung.

poem_stanzas:
A firm and flexible and gristly stuff,
That pads the joints and smooths the rubbing bone,
My nose and ear are made of me enough,
And in a shark I am a frame alone.

I have no veins to warm me, none to feed,
I heal but slowly when I am torn apart,
I am the body's firm and living bead,
The quiet cushion of the joint and ear.
ciphers.hint: Tough flexible tissue that pads joints and shapes the nose and ears.

poem_stanzas:
A dome of muscle underneath the chest,
That flattens when I pull and air comes in,
I am the bellows giving lungs their rest,
And rise again when breathing must begin.

A hiccup is a twitch upon my dome,
I part the belly from the breast above,
A shutter may share with me a name at home,
And both of us are muscles made to move.
ciphers.hint: The dome-shaped muscle below the lungs that powers breathing.

poem_stanzas:
The middle of a body, trunk and all,
Without the head that rises or the hands,
I hold the heart, the stomach, and the small
And twisting pipes the busy gut demands.

A marble figure often shows me bare,
A statue's middle with no limbs to hold,
I am the column, steady, broad, and square,
Where all the deepest organs are enrolled.
ciphers.hint: The trunk of the body, excluding the head and limbs.

poem_stanzas:
A clown of northern seas with painted beak,
That nests in burrows on a cliff's steep face,
I dive for fish and hold a crowded streak
Of silver in my bill across the race.

My cheeks are pale, my feathers black and stout,
I beat my wings and skim the northern spray,
I carry sand eels in a silver rout,
And waddle to my burrow at the day.
ciphers.hint: A black-and-white seabird with a brightly colored bill.

poem_stanzas:
A round and gentle grazer of the bay,
That drifts and munches weeds and makes no threat,
The sailors once mistook me far away
For something human that the waters met.

My snout is whiskered, flat my paddle tail,
I surf for air and sink to graze again,
A gentle giant, drifting without fail,
And cousin to a dugong in the main.
ciphers.hint: A slow, gentle aquatic mammal also called a sea cow.

poem_stanzas:
A little whale with blunt and rounded face,
That rolls and blows and chases shoals in lines,
I surf the bow-wave in a tumbling race,
And never leap as high as dolphin pines.

My teeth are spade-shaped, small my body size,
I travel in a group and speak in clicks,
I am the modest cousin that the wise
Confuse with those who leap and do the tricks.
ciphers.hint: A small, short-snouted marine mammal related to dolphins.

poem_stanzas:
A whale of Arctic ice with one long spear,
A spiralling tusk of ivory from my lip,
I rise in lanes of open water here,
And breathe where floes are splitting like a whip.

The horn the ancients sold as unicorn
Was mine, a single tooth that twists to be,
My coat is mottled grey and I am born
In Arctic seas that winter holds in fee.
ciphers.hint: A small Arctic whale with a long spiral tusk.

poem_stanzas:
A bloom that grows upon the ocean floor,
With petaled arms that sting the passing fish,
I anchor fast and wait and then devour,
And draw my crown in at the water's swish.

A clownfish shelters in my stinging arms,
A hermit crab may wear me on its back,
My name is given also to the charms
Of garden flowers round a garden track.
ciphers.hint: A flower-like sea creature with stinging tentacles.

poem_stanzas:
A pin-cushion of spines upon a rock,
That grazes kelp and clings against the surge,
A ball of needles that can bear the shock,
And hide a mouth where secret jaws emerge.

The same poor word describes a ragged child,
A barefoot waif upon a city street,
So sea and slum have shared the name, and smiled,
One spiny, one in tatters and bare feet.
ciphers.hint: A spiny sea creature, or a poor ragged child.

poem_stanzas:
A silver fish that travels home to spawn,
Against the current, leaping at each fall,
I fight the flood from dusk until the dawn,
And climb the fish-ladder or not at all.

My flesh is pink, my journey is uphill,
I dig a nest, I spawn, and then I die,
A bear will catch me at the rapids still,
And so my kind return to sea and sky.
ciphers.hint: A fish that swims upstream to spawn.

poem_stanzas:
A speckled fish that hides in cold clear streams,
With dots of black and red along my flank,
An angler casts for me and learns my schemes,
And wades in boots along the pebbled bank.

I rise for flies that dance above my pool,
A cousin to the salmon is my kin,
I love the shaded water, deep and cool,
And fast for winter when the ice comes in.
ciphers.hint: A freshwater fish with speckled sides, popular with anglers.

poem_stanzas:
A silver cloud that moves beneath the sea,
In millions travelling the water's lane,
The cod and whale and fisherman seek me,
And through the net I fall like silver rain.

A king once ate my flesh in pickled brine,
I am smoked and salted, packed in tin,
A little fish in shoals that form a line,
And every ocean feeds a silver din.
ciphers.hint: A small silvery fish that swims in huge schools.

poem_stanzas:
A flattened kite that glides above the sand,
With wings that ripple like a heavy bird,
I trail a tail with barbed and venomed brand,
That strikes the wader and the fish unheard.

I hide within the shallows, half a stone,
And bury in the mud to wait for prey,
My barbs have felled a famous hunter known,
And needled feet that dared the surf that day.
ciphers.hint: A flat fish with a venomous tail barb.

poem_stanzas:
I run the open plain on slender legs,
With horns that rise and eyes that watch for claws,
A herd of me across the grassland begs
For speed enough to outrun tooth and jaws.

A cheetah is the death that I outrace,
A sudden leap is all that I must foil,
I spring and swerve and leave no sign of place,
And skim the dust across the burning soil.
ciphers.hint: A swift, slender horned animal of the plains, like a gazelle.

poem_stanzas:
A shaggy giant of the endless grass,
With humped and heavy shoulders, horns of jet,
I travel in a thunderous, dusty mass,
And paw the snow to find the grass-life yet.

The plains once darkened with my countless kind,
The rifle thinned my herds and left me few,
My shaggy head and heavy shoulders find
A coin, a park, a name to carry through.
ciphers.hint: A large, shaggy wild ox of the North American plains.

poem_stanzas:
A slender leaper of the arid land,
With ringed and pointed horns and liquid eye,
I skim the sand and vault the stones that stand,
And leave the lion panting, heaving dry.

A poet calls a graceful thing my name,
A dancer and a ship and heedless love,
I am the swift and shy, and all the same
I leap the thorn-bush and the rocky cove.
ciphers.hint: A small, swift antelope of Africa and Asia.

poem_stanzas:
A heavy cat that swims and climbs a tree,
My coat is patterned with a ring of spots,
The jungle river holds no mystery
For me, who hunts the caiman in its plots.

A car once took my name for pride and grace,
The Maya carved my image in their stone,
I am the powerful cat of that green place,
The spotted master of a tropic throne.
ciphers.hint: A large spotted big cat of the American tropics.

poem_stanzas:
A wild and stubby cat of scrub and brush,
With mottled coat and tufted, pointed ear,
I stalk the hare and mouse and make a rush,
And vanish when a human comes too near.

My tail is short, a stub with no long sway,
A lynx is cousin to my smaller frame,
I scream at night and prowl the fading day,
And few who meet me call me by my name.
ciphers.hint: A medium wild cat of North America with a short tail and tufted ears.

poem_stanzas:
A weasel robed in brown that turns to white,
When winter folds the country in its snow,
A hunter of the rabbit, swift and slight,
I chase my quarry down its earthly hole.

A king's and bishop's ermine is my fur,
My tail is tipped in black, my temper bold,
I slay the rabbit where the heathers stir,
And wear an ermine cloak against the cold.
ciphers.hint: A small, fierce weasel that turns white in winter.

poem_stanzas:
A striped and busy hoarder of the wood,
With pockets in my cheeks for winter seed,
I fill my burrow with the pine-nut food,
And chatter at the walker in the mead.

My back is dark with lanes of pale between,
A squirrel is my red and larger kin,
I burrow under logs and wake unseen,
And stuff my cheeks before the snows begin.
ciphers.hint: A small striped rodent that stores nuts in its cheeks.

poem_stanzas:
A ring of figures drawn across the night,
Where sun and moon and planets seem to roam,
Twelve signs divide the circle's wheeling light,
And each has creatures of its starry home.

A ram, a bull, a crab, a lion, a maid,
A scale, a scorpion, archer, goat, and urn,
Two fish complete the dozen undismayed,
And every child is born beneath a turn.
ciphers.hint: A belt of constellations through which the sun and planets appear to move.

poem_stanzas:
A little pattern drawn in points of light,
A dipper or a plough or belt of three,
Too small to be a figure of the night,
Yet named by those who watch the sky with glee.

The seven sisters form a famous one,
The teapot and the northern cross are mine,
A shape no boundary holds beneath the sun,
A pattern only, drawn by human line.
ciphers.hint: A recognizable pattern of stars, smaller than a constellation.

poem_stanzas:
A region dark where nothing can return,
A well so deep that even light is snared,
A giant star collapsed, and so we learn
Of what remains when matter is not spared.

My rim is called the boundary of no return,
Around me gas goes spinning, hot and bright,
The first to image me has helped us learn
An orange ring of fire against the night.
ciphers.hint: A region of space with gravity so strong that nothing can escape.

poem_stanzas:
A tunnel in the fabric of the dark,
A shortcut joining regions far away,
A thing of theory, without any spark
Of proof, that science toys with but can't say.

The earthworm shares the first half of my name,
A gateway in a science-fiction tale,
A bridge between two points, no proof, no claim,
That no one yet has travelled or set sail.
ciphers.hint: A hypothetical tunnel through space-time linking distant points.

poem_stanzas:
A word that marks the stars and not the sun,
A day that runs a fraction short of one,
The turning of the earth against the stars,
And not the solar day when all is done.

A month and year and clock may bear my name,
The zodiac is measured by my kind,
An observatory's clock of starry fame
Keeps time against the heavens, star-defined.
ciphers.hint: Relating to the stars, especially a day measured by Earth's rotation against the stars.

poem_stanzas:
A searing pain that twists the heart within,
A torment that no medicine can still,
It grips the chest and makes the senses thin,
And turns the strongest spirit into ill.

A word for agony of mind or frame,
Akin to narrow, tight, and squeezed and sore,
I am the deepest hurt that has no name
That human hearts are fated to endure.
ciphers.hint: Severe mental or physical pain.

poem_stanzas:
A joy so large it lifts you from the ground,
A rapture that no words can fully hold,
A state in which the common sense is drowned,
And all the world is turned to shining gold.

A trance of ancient Greece once bore my name,
A standing outside of the self in bliss,
A saint and lover both may feel the same,
A transport and a rapture and a kiss.
ciphers.hint: An overwhelming feeling of great happiness or joy.

poem_stanzas:
A heat of feeling, glowing in the breast,
A zeal that burns and will not be repressed,
A passion that has put the soul to test,
And driven many to their very best.

A crowd may roar with me at some great cause,
A convert and a lover know my flame,
I am the burning heat without a pause
That lends the heart its ardour and its aim.
ciphers.hint: Intense and passionate feeling.

poem_stanzas:
A boiling anger that demands a price,
A fury that no counsel can allay,
A storm that takes the reason in a trice,
And sweeps the better judgement clean away.

A cup of poison and a serpent's crown,
A day of grapes in some old book of sin,
A deadly thing the ancients set in stone,
And one of seven that the soul lets in.
ciphers.hint: Extreme anger, often with a desire for vengeance.

poem_stanzas:
A curling of the lip, a lifted brow,
A judgment that another is beneath,
A cold disdain that will not let you bow,
And cuts the proudest with its icy teeth.

A poet calls me laughter of the proud,
A lady may be said to feel me yet,
I am the coldest of the hostile crowd,
A wound the haughty never can forget.
ciphers.hint: A feeling that someone or something is worthless or despicable.

poem_stanzas:
A shadow on the certainty of mind,
A question with no answer and no rest,
I creep behind the firmest faith you find,
And put a spider's thread within the breast.

A virtue of the sceptic, or a thief,
A Thomas will not move without my sting,
I am the crack that widens into grief,
And in the mighty make a timid thing.
ciphers.hint: A feeling of uncertainty or lack of conviction.

poem_stanzas:
To feel another's sorrow as your own,
To stand inside a stranger's heavy shoe,
To make a buried grief not quite alone,
And understand what others' tears go through.

A Greek word meaning feeling from within,
A mirror of the heart for someone's pain,
I am the bridge across the human din
That lets a fellow creature be a friend.
ciphers.hint: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

poem_stanzas:
A flat and grey indifference of heart,
A shrug that answers both the joy and woe,
A numbness where the feelings used to start,
And now no longer trouble you to know.

A word that means no passion and no care,
No pity and no anger and no love,
I am the dim and listless, empty stare
That nothing in the world can move enough.
ciphers.hint: A lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.

poem_stanzas:
A little cake that crumbles at a bite,
That ships once carried on a voyage long,
A hard and twice-baked slab to last a night,
And keep a sailor's belly from the wrong.

A plain round thing for dunking in a cup,
I come with cheese and pickle and with jam,
In parts of speech I mean a scone, and sup
With gravy in the south of where I am.
ciphers.hint: A small baked cake, usually crisp and sweet.

poem_stanzas:
A little dome that rises in a tin,
With berries folded in my golden crumb,
A breakfast that will make a morning grin,
And fill a sleepy walker's waiting drum.

A thicker round of yeast is sometimes me,
An English one is split and toasted brown,
I am the breakfast cake of blueberry,
The paper cup that never lets me down.
ciphers.hint: A small, cup-shaped quick bread, often sweet.

poem_stanzas:
A twisted knot of bread with salt to kiss,
A shape like arms across a folded breast,
A fasting food that turned to snack and bliss,
And bent the baker's arms in tangled zest.

My shape is said to echo folded prayer,
My skin is browned in lye before the bake,
I am a salty, brittle, crisp affair,
The companion of a beer or chocolate flake.
ciphers.hint: A crisp, salty knot of twisted bread.

poem_stanzas:
A cultured milk that thickens in the tub,
A tangy cream of living, unseen seed,
A cool white spoon that breakfast may convert,
And Greek or plain or fruited is my breed.

A million tiny creatures live in me,
A Turkish word has travelled with my name,
I sit in tubs and tubes beside the tea,
And help the gut and lightly feed the frame.
ciphers.hint: A thick fermented milk food.

poem_stanzas:
A bowl of grains that rattle in the box,
With milk and sugar poured upon the flakes,
A breakfast that no hungry schoolboy mocks,
And every morning in a hurry takes.

A goddess of the harvest shares my name,
A corn and wheat and oats and rice are mine,
I am a grain for morning, crisp and tame,
And in a yellow box I make the line.
ciphers.hint: A breakfast food made from processed grains.

poem_stanzas:
A sticky amber river in a jug,
That maps the pancakes with a golden coat,
A sweetness that a child will always hug,
And pour in ribbons on the waffle boat.

A maple tree will bleed me in the spring,
A cane or corn or golden beet can be,
I am the sticky, sweet, slow, glistening thing
Upon the heat. That browns the waffle free.
ciphers.hint: A thick sweet liquid, especially poured on pancakes.

poem_stanzas:
A buttery and brittle slab of sweet,
That sticks the teeth together in a wad,
A golden lump that sugar and butter meet,
And boil to make a hard and chewable pod.

A word the British use for any sweet,
A pulled and packed and paper-wrapped delight,
I am the amber of a sugared treat,
That snaps and then adheres and holds on tight.
ciphers.hint: A hard, chewy sweet made by boiling sugar and butter.

poem_stanzas:
A lattice cake that traps the butter pools,
A grid of squares that hold the syrup in,
A batter poured in heated iron tools,
And browned upon the metal grid within.

A word that also means to talk and stray,
From off the point with many a pointless phrase,
I am a crisp and golden grid in play,
The folded cake of breakfast's happy days.
ciphers.hint: A crisp batter cake with a grid of indentations.

poem_stanzas:
A sea of grass with islands here and there,
A scattering of trees upon the plain,
Where lions and gazelles and dusty air
And herds of many kinds begin again.

An acacia stands alone in me,
A wet and dry have each their yearly turn,
I am the open land where herds run free,
And wider than a meadow, hot to burn.
ciphers.hint: A grassy plain with scattered trees, as in Africa.

poem_stanzas:
A treeless plain that stretches to the sky,
A grass that runs for many a weary mile,
No hill to break the horizon climbing high,
And hardly any landmark to beguile.

A Russian word describes my grassy waste,
A horseman gallops over me alone,
A nomad rides with wind and speed and haste,
And finds no fence to hold him to a stone.
ciphers.hint: A vast, treeless grassy plain, as in Russia and Asia.

poem_stanzas:
A lonely hill with sides of sheer-cut stone,
A flat and level summit at the top,
A tower left from land the wind has thrown
Away, a monument that will not stop.

A French word underlies my name and shape,
A western film may set a chase on me,
I rise above the plain that can't escape,
A flat-topped tower on a lonely spree.
ciphers.hint: An isolated hill with steep sides and a flat top, common in the American West.

poem_stanzas:
A table in the desert, raised and broad,
With steep and rocky sides that fall away,
A level summit where the old ones trod,
And watched the sun go down across the day.

A Spanish word for table is my name,
A plateau that is smaller and alone,
I am the flat-topped height of desert fame,
Where ancient peoples built of sand and stone.
ciphers.hint: A flat-topped hill or tableland with steep sides, common in the southwest US.

poem_stanzas:
The very top of every climbing way,
The place where all the struggle finds its end,
The peak where foot and breath no longer stray,
And every step below becomes a friend.

A meeting of the leaders takes my name,
A handshake at the highest point of power,
I am the crowning point of every aim,
The final step of every climber's hour.
ciphers.hint: The highest point of a mountain.

poem_stanzas:
A little rise that sits before the great,
A stepping stone toward the towering wall,
A gentle slope that waits at mountain's gate,
And makes the climb less sudden for us all.

A city often builds upon my back,
A vineyard and an orchard share my ground,
I am the lowly spur of any track,
Before the mountain's summit can be crowned.
ciphers.hint: A low hill at the base of a mountain or mountain range.

poem_stanzas:
A tumbling stretch where white the water flies,
A roar of foam between the rocks and stones,
A place where every paddler, soaked, applies
His skill and prays against the river's groans.

A grade of white and five are used to score,
A raft and a canoe run me in line,
I hurry to the quiet stream once more,
And leave the roaring rocks and foam behind.
ciphers.hint: A fast, turbulent part of a river.

poem_stanzas:
A water falling over rocks in steps,
A stair of foam descending to a pool,
A white and tumbling ribbon that one keeps
Within the memory, beautiful and cool.

A word for anything that falling flows,
A domino can make me, and a song,
I am the mountain water that bestows
Its silver on the stones the whole day long.
ciphers.hint: A small waterfall, or a series of them.

poem_stanzas:
A little pipe of wood and silver key,
The smallest of the band and highest voiced,
My notes go up where only bats can be,
And in my reach the loudest drum rejoiced.

An Italian word for small is in my name,
A soldier's fife of old is kin to me,
I shrill the topmost melody and fame
Above an orchestra's full harmony.
ciphers.hint: A small, high-pitched flute.

poem_stanzas:
A tall and dark and wooden singing thing,
Whose double reed sits folded on a crook,
The lowest of the woodwind, I can bring
A grumbling and a jolly and a brook.

A staccato of repeated notes is fun,
A sorcerer may set me to a chase,
A grandfatherly voice, the deep and one,
That speaks in Peter's story with a face.
ciphers.hint: A large, low-pitched woodwind instrument with a double reed.

poem_stanzas:
A golden tube that slides to find the note,
A long and shining arm that moves and glides,
A bray of brass that from the bell will float
And fills the hall with sliding, brassy tides.

A word for a loudspeaker shares my name,
A jazzman and a marching band adore,
My slide can slip and glide along a frame,
And play a note that never was before.
ciphers.hint: A brass instrument with a sliding tube.

poem_stanzas:
A box of keys with bellows in between,
That breathes and wheezes as the arms divide,
A squeeze to make a chord and then a keen
That wanders through a village at its side.

A folk and street and sailor's instrument,
A metal reed that trembles in my air,
My name suggests a harmony and consent,
And two of me can marry pair by pair.
ciphers.hint: A portable instrument with bellows and keys, played by squeezing.

poem_stanzas:
A breathing bag beneath a squeezing arm,
A set of drones that hum without a rest,
I fill and squeeze and keep the chanter warm
And pull the wind to war inside my chest.

A Scottish glen and tartan own my sound,
A piper marches with me down the street,
A skin, a valve, a bag of wind is found
Where drone and chanter in a wail compete.
ciphers.hint: A wind instrument with a bag and drones, associated with Scotland.

poem_stanzas:
A wooden set of bars in careful row,
Struck by a pair of padded, bouncing beat,
A warm and hollow, dancing note below
The bright xylophone's more brittle feet.

Beneath my bars are pipes to make me warm,
A voice of Africa and southern song,
I am the wooden, resonant, soft storm
That beats a melody the whole day long.
ciphers.hint: A wooden percussion instrument with keys struck by mallets.

poem_stanzas:
A brazen circle hanging in the air,
A hammer strikes and I begin to groan,
A wave of shaking metal everywhere,
A sound that will not leave the listener alone.

A signal for a meal and for a war,
A temple and an orchestra use me,
A medal and a badge are mine once more,
And in the east I set the spirit free.
ciphers.hint: A large round metal disc struck to make a deep sound.

poem_stanzas:
A dreadful woman with a writhing head,
Whose stare can turn a living man to stone,
A hiss of serpents coiled about her dread,
And eyes that freeze a hero to the bone.

A hero with a mirror slew the chief,
Her sisters two remained and would not die,
My name describes a monstrous, awful grief,
And all who look upon me petrify.
ciphers.hint: A mythical monster whose gaze turns onlookers to stone.

poem_stanzas:
A giant of the deep beyond all scale,
A monster of the ancient, roaring main,
A whale or serpent with a monstrous tail,
That sailors swear they never see again.

A book of Job and Milton know my name,
A ship and a great nation take my word,
I am the hugest beast of any fame,
An ocean-dread, a ruler, and a word.
ciphers.hint: A biblical sea monster of enormous size.

poem_stanzas:
A land-born giant of the ancient tale,
With bones of iron and a strength like brass,
A creature of the fields that will not fail,
And feeds on mountains like a field of grass.

A big machine and business may be me,
A word for anything of monstrous size,
A land-beast of the oldest poetry,
Whose strength no spear or cleverness belies.
ciphers.hint: A huge and powerful beast, often from the book of Job.

poem_stanzas:
A dragon with two legs and leather wings,
No breath of fire, a deadly stinging tail,
A shape that heraldry and castle brings
To banners where the winds of battle sail.

I have no hindmost pair to walk the hall,
A serpent of the Welsh and English crest,
A cousin to the four-legged dragon's call,
And I am the two-legged of the nest.
ciphers.hint: A mythical dragon with two legs and wings, often with a barbed tail.

poem_stanzas:
A maiden choosing who shall fall and die,
A rider over battle with a spear,
A winged and armoured servant of the sky,
Who carries heroes from the fighting here.

They ride to Valhall with the chosen slain,
Their name means chooser of the fallen one,
A Wagner opera calls them in a strain
Of eight of them who ride about the sun.
ciphers.hint: A Norse maiden who chooses which warriors die in battle.

poem_stanzas:
A serpent of the rivers and the rain,
A hooded guardian of a temple pool,
A being half a cobra, half a man,
Who shelters with a hood the seated rule.

A race of them beneath the waters dwell,
A stone one guards a bridge and a temple door,
A southern people claim the name, and tell
Of serpents in their rivers as of yore.
ciphers.hint: A divine or semi-divine serpent being in Hindu and Buddhist mythology.

poem_stanzas:
A shower of ice that batters on the roof,
A hard and bouncing pellet, cold and round,
A storm that ruins the tender crop and hoof,
And drums a rattling music on the ground.

I fall in summer from a thundercloud,
A greeting shares my spelling and my sound,
I strike the field and on the mountains loud,
And bounce along the frozen, beaten ground.
ciphers.hint: Frozen rain falling as hard balls of ice.

poem_stanzas:
A season's turning wind that brings the rain,
A flood of sky upon the thirsty soil,
A farmer waits for me and waits in pain,
Then sows and prays and blesses all my toil.

An Arab word for season is my name,
I come to India and the southern main,
I fill the rivers, break the heat, and tame
The dust, and then I leave the land again.
ciphers.hint: A seasonal wind bringing heavy rain, especially in South Asia.

poem_stanzas:
A spinning storm of China and Japan,
A whirling wind that tears the coast apart,
A monster of the sea that wrecks the plan
And drives the water inland on the chart.

A Chinese word for great wind is in me,
A cyclone and a hurricane are kin,
I turn above the warm Pacific sea,
And carve a ruin where the coasts begin.
ciphers.hint: A violent tropical storm in the western Pacific.

poem_stanzas:
A wheel of wind around a hollow eye,
A spiral of the low and rising air,
A storm that turns the ocean to the sky,
And sets the water walking everywhere.

A bicycle in short has half my name,
A southern ocean and an Indian main,
A hurricane and typhoon are the same
Dependent on the sea that they attain.
ciphers.hint: A system of winds rotating around a low-pressure center.

poem_stanzas:
A roaring storm with names of men and maids,
That comes in from the sea with walls of rain,
A season of the warm Atlantic trades,
And leaves a coast in ruin and in pain.

A Carib god once lent me half my name,
A storm that climbs from one to five in scale,
I am the wind that drowns the strongest flame
Of any ship that dares to meet my gale.
ciphers.hint: A violent tropical storm with strong winds, in the Atlantic.

poem_stanzas:
A violent wind that rages and uproots,
A storm of Shakespeare and a ship at sea,
A roaring that will trample all the fruits,
And rattle every window in the lea.

A teapot may contain me in a phrase,
An overture of Tchaikovsky bears my name,
I am the furious wind of old and rocky days,
A storm of Shakespeare and of shipwreck's fame.
ciphers.hint: A violent windy storm.

poem_stanzas:
A flood that covers all the drowned ground,
A rain that will not stop for forty days,
A boat upon the water may be found,
And every hill is hidden in the haze.

A story of a patriarch and ark,
A word for any overwhelming flood,
I am the water rising over dark,
And all the earth is swallowed in the mud.
ciphers.hint: A great flood, or a heavy downpour.

poem_stanzas:
A season when the rain forgets to fall,
The cracked and dusty earth, the empty well,
The farmer staring at the ruined all,
A whisper of a hot and weary spell.

A dust-bowl and a famine are my kin,
A dryness that can wither any field,
I am the long and thirsty, parched within,
The empty-seeming sky that will not yield.
ciphers.hint: A long period of unusually low rainfall.

poem_stanzas:
A little blade with handle for the hand,
A mason spreads the mortar with my flat,
A gardener digs a hole in soft brown land,
And pats a plant to settle it like that.

A mason's tool and gardener's tool am I,
A silver one may cut a turf or sod,
I lay a brick and set a seedling by,
And serve the bricklayer and the garden clod.
ciphers.hint: A small hand tool with a flat blade used for digging or spreading.

poem_stanzas:
A crescent blade with handle short and plain,
That sweeps a swath of barley, wheat, and rye,
A harvest tool that bends and cuts the grain,
And leaves the golden stubble standing by.

A hammer crossed with me is revolution,
A moon and reaper's shape are mine to lend,
I am the curved and shining execution
Of harvest when the summer comes to end.
ciphers.hint: A curved blade with a short handle used for cutting grain.

poem_stanzas:
A blade that bites and turns the heavy earth,
A farmer drags me behind horse or team,
I open furrows for the seed's rebirth,
And break the clods of winter in a seam.

A starry pattern shares my name on high,
A wagon and a Big Bear are the same,
I am the field-tool underneath the sky,
That makes a field of any fallow claim.
ciphers.hint: A farm tool with a blade that turns over soil.

poem_stanzas:
A broad and flat and metal scoop of steel,
With handle long to save the bending back,
I lift the earth and coal and sand and meal,
And pile it in a heap beside the track.

A spade and me are near and often mixed,
I move the loose, a spade divides the ground,
I am the scoop of every road that's fixed,
And every grave and every snow-piled mound.
ciphers.hint: A tool with a broad blade for digging and lifting.

poem_stanzas:
A head of iron with a point and spike,
Upon a handle swung above the crown,
I crack the rock and split the frozen dike,
And bring the hard and stony matter down.

A miner and a roadman and a trench,
A prospector in hills of gold and ore,
I break the crust of every rocky bench,
And open up the mountain's hidden door.
ciphers.hint: A tool with a curved iron head, used to break rock and hard ground.

poem_stanzas:
A metal jaw that grips a stubborn nut,
A lever arm to turn it tight or slack,
A mechanic's tool for every bolt and strut,
That will not yield until I bend it back.

A twist of pain and parting shares my name,
A monkey and a pipe and socket too,
I am the grip that answers every claim
Of threaded bolt and rusted, stubborn screw.
ciphers.hint: A tool for gripping and turning nuts and bolts.

poem_stanzas:
A pair of jaws upon a pivot pin,
That grip and bend and twist a stubborn wire,
A tool that lets the weakest fingers win,
And cut and pull and shape a metal briar.

A cousin to the tongs and to the shears,
A wire and a nail are mine to hold,
I wear a rubber handle, calm the fears
Of shocks, and bend the metal, hot or cold.
ciphers.hint: A hand tool with jaws for gripping and bending wire.

poem_stanzas:
A frame with threads that rise and fall in time,
A shuttle flying through the open shed,
A weaver works to rhythm and to rhyme,
And cloth is born of warp and weft and thread.

I hang above a weaver like a threat,
A verb for something huge that looms in view,
I am the frame where warp and weft have met,
And every pattern of the cloth comes true.
ciphers.hint: A machine for weaving cloth.

poem_stanzas:
A slender rod that twists the wool to thread,
A whorl of weight to make it spin and turn,
A sleeping princess pricked her hand and bled,
And from that prick a kingdom's sleep did earn.

A part of any axle that rotates,
A wooden spike upon a stair or chair,
A slender shape that history relates,
And sleeping beauty's finger met it there.
ciphers.hint: A slender rod used to spin thread, or a rotating part.

poem_stanzas:
A brother of an element, the same,
But heavier or lighter by a bit,
A different weight that bears a single name,
And in the nucleus the difference sit.

A scientist can make me in a pile,
A carbon and a hydrogen have kin,
I may be steady or I may be vile,
And half of me will vanish from within.
ciphers.hint: A version of an element with a different number of neutrons.

poem_stanzas:
A packet of the light without a mass,
That travels at the fastest speed of all,
A wave and yet a dot of light, alas,
And when it strikes the eye the sight will call.

A tender plant may grow toward my ray,
A quantum is my measure, small and bright,
I carry energy from sun to day,
And make the world a visible delight.
ciphers.hint: A particle of light.

poem_stanzas:
A helper in a chemical affair,
That speeds the change and yet remains the same,
A key that opens without wear or tear,
And never is consumed within the flame.

A person who begins a change in state,
An enzyme is a living one of me,
I hurry on the change and keep my weight,
And leave the reaction as it had to be.
ciphers.hint: A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up.

poem_stanzas:
A liquid that can make a solid flee,
A liquid where another will dissolve,
The water is the commonest of me,
And in a bath a stain will not survive.

A word for one who pays a debt as well,
A chemistry for paint and glue and dye,
I am the bath where hidden powders dwell,
And make a liquid of the mud thereby.
ciphers.hint: A liquid that dissolves other substances.

poem_stanzas:
A giant chain of small and linked repeats,
A plastic and a protein and a starch,
A molecule of many tiny feats,
That builds a fibre, sheet, or bottle's arch.

Two Greek words meaning many parts are mine,
A rubber and a nylon and a glue,
I am the long and knitted, twisted line,
That gives a plastic bottle its value.
ciphers.hint: A large molecule made of many repeated small units.

poem_stanzas:
A preparation that will teach the blood,
A taste of illness, weakened, dead, or cracked,
A shield against the coming of the flood,
And all the fever that the years have tracked.

A cow's disease and Jenner gave my fame,
A needle and a card record my deed,
I spare a child the fever and the shame,
And make a population safe from need.
ciphers.hint: A preparation that trains the immune system against a disease.

poem_stanzas:
The whole instruction written in a cell,
The alphabet of four that shapes a life,
A book of all the body's lore and spell,
And every inherited of joy and strife.

A project mapped a human one with care,
A double spiral holds me in its coil,
A code of four that every creature share,
And keeps a species from the mortal spoil.
ciphers.hint: The complete set of genetic material in an organism.

poem_stanzas:
A laziness of matter in a state,
A body will not move unless it's forced,
And once it moves will keep its speed and rate,
Until another power has it coursed.

A Latin word for idle is my root,
A Newton laid me down in famous law,
A resting thing and moving thing salute,
And neither turns without a sudden flaw.
ciphers.hint: The tendency of an object to resist changes in its motion.

poem_stanzas:
A game upon a pony at a canter,
A mallet and a ball and pounding hoof,
A field of grass where riders chase and banter,
And strike the wooden ball through goal and proof.

A shirt with a short collar shares my name,
A water sport with horses made of air,
A prince and a plantation played the game,
And fields of turf are rich and green and rare.
