ciphers.hint: A ball game played on horseback.

poem_stanzas:
A game of light and feather, net and racket,
A shuttlecock that hovers and then drops,
A gentle arc that has a graceful bracket,
And volleys that go on and never stop.

A stately home once gave the game its name,
A pastime played within a garden hall,
I am the swiftest sport of feathered aim,
Where shuttlecocks arise and never fall.
ciphers.hint: A racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a net.

poem_stanzas:
A sliding down a mountainside of white,
On boards of wood or fibreglass and steel,
A rush of cold and speed and pure delight,
And every turn a balance and a feel.

A Nordic and an alpine are my kinds,
A pole and boot and binding hold me tight,
A downhill racer and a jump of winds,
And I am winter's swift and shining flight.
ciphers.hint: The sport of gliding over snow on long boards.

poem_stanzas:
A sport of vault and beam and bars and rings,
Of somersaults and balance and of grace,
Of bodies flying, twisting, turning things,
And chalk that marks the hand and marks the face.

A Greek word for the naked and the gym,
A horse with pommels and a floor of springs,
A vault and a full twist and every limb,
And all the strength and stretch of human things.
ciphers.hint: A sport of acrobatic exercises performed on apparatus.

poem_stanzas:
A game of diamond, innings, bat and glove,
A pitcher and a catcher and a throw,
A home run and a crowd that roars above,
And nine men in a field of dust and woe.

A national pastime of the States,
A series and a seventh-inning stretch,
A strike and ball and out and run and plates,
And every fan a hero in the sketch.
ciphers.hint: A bat-and-ball game with innings and bases.

poem_stanzas:
A game of serve and volley and of net,
Of setting up a spike above the sand,
A ball that must not touch the ground as yet,
And six on either side who understand.

A beach and an Olympic game are mine,
A bump and a rotation and a block,
A name of fly and ball and net and line,
And every point begins with a hard knock.
ciphers.hint: A game in which two teams hit a ball over a net by hand.

poem_stanzas:
A game of bounce and dribble, hoop and net,
Of giants leaping high to slam and score,
A court of wood where every foul and threat,
And every pass is measured at the door.

A peach basket once gave the game its name,
A maple floor and sneakers make it squeak,
A three and a free throw and all the same,
And all the waiting crowd begins to shriek.
ciphers.hint: A game with hoops and a bouncing ball.

poem_stanzas:
A game of greens and flags and little holes,
Of clubs and tees and carts and quiet talk,
Of patience that a walker in him rolls,
And drives a tiny ball along the park.

A Scottish word for strike has made my name,
A bird and a bogey and a par to beat,
A hole in one remains my finest flame,
And every player blames his wandering feet.
ciphers.hint: A game of hitting a small ball into holes with clubs.

poem_stanzas:
The bell that calls the brothers to their prayer,
The cloister and the arches tall and grey,
A place of silence and of holy care,
Where monks have knelt and watched the dawning day.

An abbot rules a house of this design,
A ruined one may stand with roofless nave,
The kings of England once were crowned in mine,
And pilgrims travelled far my walls to have.
ciphers.hint: A monastery or church ruled by an abbot or abbess.

poem_stanzas:
A subtle snake that hides among the fern,
With zigzag markings down a slender back,
A sudden strike that few have time to learn,
A venom in a mouth of velvet black.

I have no limbs and yet I glide and hiss,
I bask upon the heath in summer's prime,
A saint is said to drive my kind from bliss,
And yet I add a number in a rhyme.
ciphers.hint: A small venomous snake, the only venomous reptile in Britain.

poem_stanzas:
A tree that loves the water and the fen,
With rounded leaves and catkins in the spring,
My timber turns to red when cut, and then
The clogs and charcoal of the old world bring.

Along the brook I stand with roots in mud,
A cousin to the birch and to the willow,
My wood is pale and colours when it's cut,
And dykes and dams are mine to hold and hallow.
ciphers.hint: A tree of damp ground with toothed leaves and catkins.

poem_stanzas:
A golden stone that is not stone at all,
The hardened tears of trees that lived of old,
A window on a fly that had a fall,
A treasure that the Baltic traders sold.

My hue has named a traffic light and more,
A million years have made me hard and clear,
A little insect sleeps within my core,
And jewellery has worn me many a year.
ciphers.hint: Fossilized tree resin, often golden and used in jewellery.

poem_stanzas:
A branching crown of bone upon a brow,
That falls away when winter takes the wood,
The stag that wears me grows and sheds me now,
And uses me to push where rivals stood.

A hollow horn is never kin to me,
For I am bone and branched and shed each year,
A manor hall may hang a wall with me,
And hunters count the points that I may bear.
ciphers.hint: A branched horn grown by a stag and shed each year.

poem_stanzas:
A cloth that ties about the waist and front,
To keep the cooking and the paint at bay,
A butcher and a mason wear my brunt,
A child at school may wear me every day.

An airport shares my name upon its field,
A stage extends in front of every scene,
I am the guard that cook and workman wield,
And I have kept a hundred dresses clean.
ciphers.hint: A garment worn over the front of the body to keep clothes clean.

poem_stanzas:
A leafy roof on pillars in the shade,
A bower where the roses climb and meet,
A seat of rest that garden hands have made,
A cool retreat where summer walks are sweet.

A Latin word for tree is at my root,
A branch of it is grafted for the fruit,
I am the shaded nook where lovers suit,
And vines and roses twine about my foot.
ciphers.hint: A shady garden shelter formed by trees or a trellis.

poem_stanzas:
A slender tree whose leaves are never still,
They quiver though the air be calm and warm,
A whisper runs across them on the hill,
And shivers tell the coming of a storm.

My bark is pale and marked as if with eyes,
My wood is soft and turned to matches, bright,
The slightest wind will set my leaves to rise,
And tremble in the day and through the night.
ciphers.hint: A poplar tree whose leaves tremble in the slightest breeze.

poem_stanzas:
A book of maps that holds the world in leaves,
A giant who must bear the sky on high,
The first of these a scholar's hand achieves,
The second is a Titan in the sky.

A mountain and a vertebra are mine,
A Titan and a book of maps as well,
I hold the world, or draw it line by line,
The bearer and the book that charts and tells.
ciphers.hint: A book of maps, or a mythical giant who holds up the sky.

poem_stanzas:
A room beneath the sloping of the roof,
Where dust and old belongings find a home,
A hiding place from feet and eyes aloof,
A where-a-child-might-climb and be alone.

A Greek region gives me half my name,
A capital of Greece, a columned style,
I store the trunks and treasures of the same,
And spiders spin their webs upon the tile.
ciphers.hint: The space or room just under the roof of a house.

poem_stanzas:
A stretch of canvas over door and shop,
That keeps the sun and rain from passers-by,
A striped and sloping sheet that shops will prop,
To shade the fruit and keep the pavement dry.

A caravan puts out a cloth like mine,
A boat may wear me over cockpit small,
I give a shadow at the shop-front sign,
And shelter those who wait within my fall.
ciphers.hint: A sheet of canvas stretched to give shade.

poem_stanzas:
A shade of blue that names a cloudless sky,
The colour of the heaven when it clears,
The field of many a coat of arms on high,
The tint of distant hills the sailor steers.

A French word underlies my name and hue,
A jewel shares the shade of what I am,
I am the blue of sky and distance too,
And shyness takes my name for his alarm.
ciphers.hint: A bright blue colour; the unclouded sky.

poem_stanzas:
A giant grass that rises straight and tall,
With hollow joints and woody, hardened stem,
A panda's food, a scaffold on a wall,
A raft and pipe and scaffolding and gem.

I have no rings of growth as trees have done,
A panda and a builder both agree,
I grow so fast I stand before the sun,
And in a single season, tall as tree.
ciphers.hint: A tall, hollow tropical grass used for building and food.

poem_stanzas:
A bearded grain that ripples in the field,
A cousin to the wheat and to the rye,
I fill the bin and malt the whisky's yield,
And make the bread that keeps the winter dry.

My name appears in water and in soup,
A book of Ruth has me within its tale,
I am the humbler grain of field and group,
And in the malt I turn the beer to ale.
ciphers.hint: A cereal grain used for food, malt, and whisky.

poem_stanzas:
A dark and heavy stone of molten birth,
That cooled and shrank in pillars tall and straight,
The Giant's Road that runs on Irish earth,
Is made of me in hexagonal estate.

The ocean floor and moon are paved with me,
The lava cools and hardens into stone,
I am the grey of cliffs beside the sea,
And darkest rock the fiery hills have thrown.
ciphers.hint: A dark, fine-grained volcanic rock.

poem_stanzas:
A fire upon a hill to warn or guide,
A light that tells of danger or of shore,
A chain of them across the countryside,
That carried news of ships and war and more.

A hill and a New England town bear me,
A television mast may send my ray,
A burning signal on the land or sea,
That warns the ships or shows the safe home way.
ciphers.hint: A fire or light set up on a hill as a signal.

poem_stanzas:
A bird of omen in a Beatles song,
A common thrush with golden bill and eye,
That sings from rooftops when the nights are long,
And carols from the chimney to the sky.

My mate is brown and I am dark as jet,
I whistle from the rooftops in the spring,
I was baked in a famous pie, and yet
I am the common bird whose songs take wing.
ciphers.hint: A common dark thrush with a yellow bill and melodious song.

poem_stanzas:
A soft and stretching bag within the frame,
That holds a fluid till the body's call,
A hollow organ that has no other name,
And lies within the pelvis, low and small.

A floating seaweed shares my name at sea,
A word for boastful talk is also mine,
A sack of fluid stored inside of me,
The surgeon and the body both design.
ciphers.hint: The organ that stores urine.

poem_stanzas:
A cap that ties beneath the chin with string,
A baby and a lady wore the same,
A Highland one with ribbons is a thing,
And babes and dames will wear me all the same.

A car's front cover borrows now my name,
A hood in Britain, hinged to lift and close,
A Scottish soldier wears me, and the same
A word for calm and peace the sailor knows.
ciphers.hint: A hat tied under the chin, or a car's front cover.

poem_stanzas:
A thorny tangle in the hedgerow side,
That scratches hands and catches wool and sleeve,
Whose berries ripen dark at harvest-tide,
And leave the forager with stains to grieve.

My fruit is black and sweet in autumn sun,
A briar and a rose are kin to me,
I am the prickly bush where berries run,
And jam and wine and crumble come of me.
ciphers.hint: A prickly wild shrub, especially the blackberry bush.

poem_stanzas:
A golden metal made of two at least,
A copper and a zinc combined in heat,
A trumpet and a doorknob and a beast,
A monument that stands in every street.

A boldness and a nerve are called by me,
A band of wind and horn plays in my tone,
I am the alloy that the world can see,
And polish bright as any kingly throne.
ciphers.hint: A yellow alloy of copper and zinc.

poem_stanzas:
A little block of baked and hardened clay,
That stacks in courses into wall and house,
A mason lays me level day by day,
And mortar holds me quiet as a mouse.

A colour and a sturdy person may
Be called my name, a solid thing and plain,
A wall of me will stand for many a day,
And hold a house against the wind and rain.
ciphers.hint: A rectangular block of baked clay used for building.

poem_stanzas:
A set of straps upon a horse's head,
The bit between the teeth, the rein in hand,
A rider's means of where the beast is led,
A check upon a temper in the land.

A curb and a restraint are called by me,
To check one's tongue is to be bridled so,
The saddler and the rider both agree,
I turn the willing horse the way to go.
ciphers.hint: The headgear of straps and bit used to control a horse.

poem_stanzas:
A metal of the oldest age of man,
A copper mixed with tin to make me strong,
A medal and a statue and a pan,
A colour and a third-place prize ere long.

My age came after stone and before steel,
A tan and a third medal wear my hue,
The athlete on the lowest step will feel
My weight, and yet be glad the race is through.
ciphers.hint: An alloy of copper and tin, or a brown colour.

poem_stanzas:
A round and shining skin of air and soap,
That floats and trembles, rainbow-tinted, bright,
A thing of fragile and translucent hope,
That breaks at one small touch of finger's might.

A market and a rumour may be mine,
An economic one may swell and burst,
A child will chase me in the summer shine,
And blow a wand to make me, not the worst.
ciphers.hint: A thin sphere of liquid enclosing air.

poem_stanzas:
A metal clasp that holds a belt or shoe,
A tongue that fits a hole and keeps it tight,
A soldier wears me where his gear hangs true,
And horses' harness jingles in the night.

A knee may give and fold and so be mine,
To yield and give way is to share my name,
I hold a strap and keep the waist in line,
And in a storm I hold the gear the same.
ciphers.hint: A clasp for fastening a belt or strap.

poem_stanzas:
A song of joy that people sing together,
With holly and a wassail in the hall,
A season and a surname I wear either,
And children sing me at the doors of all.

A Christmas round and a girl's name as well,
A dance and a refrain are mine to hold,
I am the happy song that bells will tell,
And winter hears me sung against the cold.
ciphers.hint: A joyful song, especially one sung at Christmas.

poem_stanzas:
A stone stronghold with battlements and keep,
A moat and a portcullis and a wall,
A place where lords and ladies used to sleep,
And guards looked out to see the foemen fall.

A chess piece shaped like me can move and take,
A sand one children build beside the sea,
I am the fortress that the masons make,
And many a tale of sieges lives in me.
ciphers.hint: A large fortified building with thick walls and towers.

poem_stanzas:
A hollow in the rock both deep and vast,
With stalactites that hang like frozen tears,
A place of dripping dark where echoes last,
And hidden rivers run through unseen years.

A philosopher has likened men to me,
A hidden hoard of pirates may be mine,
A hollow in the rock the guides will see,
And lamps are lit to let the tourists shine.
ciphers.hint: A large cave or a vast underground chamber.

poem_stanzas:
A fragrant tree of Lebanon and song,
Whose timber scents the chest and builds the door,
A mountain conifer both straight and strong,
That shelters birds and shades the forest floor.

A poet feeds his bees in one of mine,
A chest of drawers may breathe my fragrant wood,
I am the evergreen of ancient line,
That stood upon the mountains where I stood.
ciphers.hint: A large evergreen tree with fragrant, durable wood.

poem_stanzas:
A room beneath the level of the street,
Where wine and coal and winter stores are kept,
A cool and dark and echoing retreat,
Where spiders work and bottles lie and slept.

A door within a floor may lead to me,
A salt or a great storm may bear my name,
I am the underground where things can be,
And cool for apples, wine, and storing's aim.
ciphers.hint: A room below ground used for storage or wine.

poem_stanzas:
A golden cup with jewels at the rim,
That holds the wine of sacred rite and prayer,
A poet dreams of one no hand can dim,
A vessel that the holy hands will bear.

A grail of Arthur's knights and faith am I,
A flower and a cup may share my name,
I hold the sacred wine beneath the sky,
And poets seek me as an endless flame.
ciphers.hint: A large ornate cup used to hold wine in ceremonies.

poem_stanzas:
A two-wheeled car of battle and of race,
Whose horse-borne wheels go thunderous round the track,
A rider standing in a swaying place,
With reins and dust and never looking back.

A sun-god drives me daily through the sky,
A prophet rode a fiery one on high,
A Roman cheered the turning wheels nearby,
And Ben-Hur raced in me to victory.
ciphers.hint: A two-wheeled vehicle pulled by horses, used in ancient racing and war.

poem_stanzas:
A stack of brick that rises from the roof,
That lifts the smoke away from hearth and flame,
A sweep will climb me with a brush and proof,
And Santa finds me in the winter's game.

A sweep and Mary Poppins both may know me,
A factory stack may tower and smoke and steep,
A stork will nest upon the top and show me,
And winter smoke goes up while embers sleep.
ciphers.hint: A vertical pipe that carries smoke from a fire.

poem_stanzas:
A drink of apple pressed and left to work,
A golden and a cloudy and a dry,
A Somerset and a Devon farmhand's quirk,
A cup of autumn in a glass gone by.

A vinegar of mine is sweet and tart,
A press and an old orchard are my home,
A wassail bowl may warm my winter heart,
And apples give me all the juice I roam.
ciphers.hint: A drink made from fermented apple juice.

poem_stanzas:
A black and burned remainder of a fire,
A glowing ember falling in the grate,
A grey and dusty thing when flames retire,
A trackside of a locomotive's freight.

A princess sweeps me, and a track is made,
A Cinderella scrubs me from the floor,
A volcano throws me when it has laid
Its fury down, and asks for nothing more.
ciphers.hint: A piece of burnt coal or wood that no longer flames.

poem_stanzas:
A stronghold on the summit of a town,
The last defence when walls have fallen low,
A place of refuge when the foe comes down,
Where soldiers make a final, stubborn show.

A book and a magazine may bear my name,
A TV series took my word for fame,
I am the fortress at the height's last claim,
Where drums once beat and fell and beat the same.
ciphers.hint: A fortress, usually on high ground, protecting a city.

poem_stanzas:
A little plant of meadow and of lawn,
With trefoil leaves that cattle love to eat,
A lucky one with four may yet be born,
And bees will find me honey-sweet and fleet.

A shamrock and a trefoil are my kin,
A patriotic flower of Erin's land,
A grazing field is where my roots begin,
And children search for four-leaf in the sand.
ciphers.hint: A low plant with three-lobed leaves, often found in meadows.

poem_stanzas:
A metal grey and hard and often blue,
That colours glass and paint a deep, rich shade,
A word for goblins is my old name too,
A battery and a magnet I have made.

A shade of blue and a metal share my name,
A goblin gave me my old German word,
I harden steel and colour glass the same,
And strengthen every magnet's hidden cord.
ciphers.hint: A hard silver-white metal used in blue pigments.

poem_stanzas:
A silver net that morning dew makes plain,
A trap of silk spun out of spider's thread,
A dusty veil on beams and window-pane,
A snare where little flies are caught and dead.

A dusty corner holds me in the house,
The word has come to mean a thing grown stale,
A broom will sweep me where the spiders drowse,
And time will wear me thin and pale and frail.
ciphers.hint: A spider's web, especially an old and dusty one.

poem_stanzas:
A reddish metal ductile, soft, and warm,
That carries wire and roof and coin and bell,
A kettle and a statue take my form,
And conductors of lightning in me dwell.

A coin and a policeman share my name,
A green that weather brings upon my roof,
I am the metal that the wires claim,
And in a penny I am not aloof.
ciphers.hint: A reddish-brown metal used for wire and coins.

poem_stanzas:
A deep and heavy red of blood and rose,
The colour of a king and cardinal,
A stain upon the cheek that anger shows,
A tide that dyes the evening sky and all.

A royal and a rock and a worm are mine,
A word for red the poets use for dread,
I am the deepest red of summer wine,
The colour of the dying day ahead.
ciphers.hint: A rich deep red colour.

poem_stanzas:
A garden flower with many pointed leaves,
A Mexican of mountain and of sun,
A bloom that autumn on the stalk achieves,
And shows the gardener what her hands have won.

A Swedish botanist has left my name,
A ballerina and a lake may hold it too,
I am the tall and brilliant bloom of flame,
In every colour but the sky's own blue.
ciphers.hint: A showy garden flower with many petals, native to Mexico.

poem_stanzas:
A golden sun upon a hollow stem,
That turns to silver when the seeds take flight,
A child will blow and scatter all of them,
And wish a wish beneath the summer light.

A lion's tooth has named me in the French,
A salad leaf and wine are mine as well,
The children call me clock upon the bench,
And puff my sphere and ring no bell.
ciphers.hint: A yellow weed that becomes a round puffball of seeds.

poem_stanzas:
A gentle bird of peace and of the ark,
That brought the olive leaf to Noah's hand,
A symbol that the sky is no more dark,
A cooing voice above the weary land.

A symbol and a chocolate share my name,
A turtle and a mourning are my kind,
A goddess and a god have known my fame,
And peace is what the world has hoped to find.
ciphers.hint: A stocky seed-eating bird, a symbol of peace.

poem_stanzas:
A green and precious stone of vivid hue,
A beryl that the Spanish conquerors sought,
A city and an isle have borrowed my name too,
A jewel that a queen or king has bought.

A wizard's city shares my name in green,
A shade of green as vivid as the spring,
I am the precious stone of vivid sheen,
And birth-stone of a month and many a ring.
ciphers.hint: A bright green precious stone.

poem_stanzas:
A tale of talking beasts with meaning hid,
A tortoise and a hare and one who wins,
A moral for a child beneath the lid,
A lesson dressed in feathers and in grins.

A slave of Greece has left a store of me,
A compiler and a lie may share my name,
A short and pointed story is my key,
And animals have made my endless fame.
ciphers.hint: A short story with a moral, often told of beasts that speak.

poem_stanzas:
A little lantern of the summer night,
That drifts and winks above the meadow grass,
A beetle with a body full of light,
That signals in the dark to lad or lass.

A folk song puts a cow and me in rhyme,
A summer evening twinkles where I pass,
A living, cold, and silent light is mine,
That turns the meadows into fields of glass.
ciphers.hint: A beetle that glows in the dark to attract mates.

poem_stanzas:
A print of something that has long been dead,
A leaf or shell or bone within the stone,
A story that the layers left unsaid,
A record of a creature no one's known.

A word for one grown old and set and strange,
A fuel that is buried, dark and slow,
I am the ancient life that time could not estrange,
A stone that holds the shape of long ago.
ciphers.hint: The preserved remains of an ancient plant or animal in rock.

poem_stanzas:
A monstrous face that juts from tower and wall,
A spout with open mouth and horn and claw,
A guardian who watches over all,
And turns the rain from off the roofs that awe.

A cathedral and a castle wear my kind,
A spout that keeps the walls from rain and rot,
A monster that the masons left behind,
To scare the devil from the holy spot.
ciphers.hint: A grotesque carved stone creature on a building, often a waterspout.

poem_stanzas:
A printed sheet of news and notices,
A journal where official matters dwell,
A word from Venice for the coin one pays,
A newspaper that tells the town's own tale.

A London paper bears my name today,
To publish is to put me into print,
I am the sheet that tells the world the way,
And every notice in me leaves a hint.
ciphers.hint: A newspaper or official journal.

poem_stanzas:
A knotted root of hot and fragrant spice,
A pale and pungent rhizome underground,
That warms the winter punch and pudding nice,
And gives the Christmas biscuit its own sound.

A cat of orange fur may share my name,
A girl with fiery hair is called by me,
I am the root the baker loves the same,
And ale and beer have known my spicing glee.
ciphers.hint: A hot, fragrant root used as a spice.

poem_stanzas:
A faint and trembling light upon the dark,
A hint of dawn before the sun is up,
A little shine that leaves a silver mark,
The last of daylight in a shaded cup.

A hope and an interest may be mine,
A word for something faintly seen and shy,
I am the weak and silver, wavering shine,
That keeps a little comfort in the sky.
ciphers.hint: A faint or unsteady light.

poem_stanzas:
A cup with stem and foot and rounded bowl,
A vessel for a toast of wine or ale,
A golden thing that shepherds once would hold,
A treasure in a tale of holy grail.

A drum and a cup and a bird may share
A part of my name, a stemmed and shining thing,
I hold a toast to joy or to despair,
And drink the health of beggar and of king.
ciphers.hint: A drinking cup with a stem and a base.

poem_stanzas:
A hard and speckled rock of quartz and mica,
A stubborn stone that builders love to use,
A monument and a kitchen counter like a
Boulder, and a pavement for the shoes.

A state and a great hill may bear my name,
A word for stubborn is akin to mine,
I am the speckled stone of grey and flame,
That weathers into soil where grow the pine.
ciphers.hint: A hard, coarse-grained igneous rock.

poem_stanzas:
A crunch of little stones beneath the shoe,
A path of grey and dusty, shifting bits,
A drive of me the gardener will strew,
A bed of me where water slowly sits.

A churchyard and a grave may share my word,
A voice grown rough and hoarse is like to me,
I am the crunch of stones in paths that's heard,
And gardens spread me under shrub and tree.
ciphers.hint: Loose stones used for paths and drives.

poem_stanzas:
A little cave of beauty or of prayer,
A cool and secret chamber in the rock,
A place of blue and green with water there,
Where tourists and the faithful come to look.

A sea one in Capri draws the crowd,
A garden one is built with shells and stone,
An Italian word for cave is mine, and proud,
A hidden shrine where prayers have long been known.
ciphers.hint: A small picturesque cave or a cave-like shrine.

poem_stanzas:
A narrow channel cut by running rain,
A little gorge between the banks of clay,
That carries off the storm across the plain,
And deepens with the water's slow way.

A cricket ground has one behind the wicket,
A noun for a small valley is my kind,
I am the earthen ditch where storms have bitten,
And water cuts the soil it leaves behind.
ciphers.hint: A water-worn ravine or channel.

poem_stanzas:
A little cluster round a village green,
A church, an inn, and half a score of homes,
A quiet place where everyone is seen,
And nobody but nobody far roams.

A prince of Denmark shares my name in play,
A Shakespeare hero and a village too,
I am the smallest settlement that may
Have fields and lanes and a believing pew.
ciphers.hint: A small settlement or village.

poem_stanzas:
A purple carpet on the lonely moor,
A low and woody shrub of wind and stone,
That bees and grouse and walkers all adore,
And makes a honey that is all its own.

A Scottish song and a colour share my name,
A heath and a moor are mine to clothe and hold,
I am the purple bloom of wildest fame,
That turns the hills of Scotland into gold.
ciphers.hint: A low evergreen shrub with purple flowers, common on moors.

poem_stanzas:
A gas so light it lifts a balloon,
A second element upon the chart,
A voice that rises to a comic tune,
A word from Greek for sun and placed apart.

I filled the first great airship long ago,
I cool the magnets that the doctors use,
A party gas that makes the voices go
Up high, the lightest atom none can lose.
ciphers.hint: A light, colourless gas used to fill balloons.

poem_stanzas:
A hardwood tree of North America,
With shaggy bark and nuts the squirrels hide,
A timber for the handle and the fire,
A wood that swings an axe with steady pride.

A folk expression uses my name for true,
A president and a town may bear it too,
A smoke of mine will flavour meat for you,
And boys have swung a bat of me in view.
ciphers.hint: A North American tree with hard wood and edible nuts.

poem_stanzas:
A little valley in the wooded land,
A cup of earth with sides of gentle grass,
A place where trees and shadows understand,
And echoes of a distant footfall pass.

A tree may have me in its trunk and be
A home for owl and squirrel and for bee,
An empty space and an echoing sound,
Are both my name, as every child can see.
ciphers.hint: A small valley or a hole in something.

poem_stanzas:
A dagger hanging from the eaves of ice,
That grows when days are warm and nights are cold,
A silver spike that melts and drips precise,
A frozen tear the winter likes to hold.

A pendant and a crystal may be mine,
A cold and backward thing may bear my word,
I hang upon the eaves in winter's line,
And drip to nothing when the spring is heard.
ciphers.hint: A hanging spike of ice formed by dripping water.

poem_stanzas:
A dome of blocks of hardened snow and ice,
A shelter in the Arctic's wind and cold,
A rounded house that hunters build precise,
Where families are warm within its fold.

An Inuit has shaped me with a knife,
A word from their own language forms my name,
I am the rounded shelter of the north,
That keeps the darkness and the drift at bay.
ciphers.hint: A dome-shaped shelter built from blocks of snow.

poem_stanzas:
A deep and dusk-blue shade of violet-blue,
A dye that India sent across the sea,
A rainbow colour at the outer few,
A plant that stains the vat of mystery.

A spectrum word that sits by violet,
A blue that dyes the denim of the world,
A child and a great trade have known my threat,
And ships of mine across the ocean hurled.
ciphers.hint: A deep blue-violet colour, or the plant yielding it.

poem_stanzas:
A pale and creamy substance of the tusk,
A tower and a gate and a piano key,
A carving and a chessman in the dusk,
A colour of an age of elegy.

A coast of Africa has taken my name,
A trade in tusks has brought the elephant harm,
I am the pale and polished white of fame,
That carved the throne and carved the lady's arm.
ciphers.hint: A hard, creamy-white substance from tusks, or its colour.

poem_stanzas:
A fragrant flower of the warmer air,
A climbing shrub of white and yellow bloom,
A scent that women weave into their hair,
A tea that scents a room and fills the gloom.

A Disney princess and a rice both bear
My name, a perfume and a night of heat,
I am the blossom of the evening air,
Whose fragrance makes the dark complete.
ciphers.hint: A shrub with fragrant white or yellow flowers.

poem_stanzas:
An opaque stone of quartz in many hues,
A red and brown and green and darkly veined,
A gem that ancient seal-carvers would choose,
A name that many a boy and man has gained.

A gemstone in the Bible's city wall,
A national park in Canada bears my name,
I am a form of quartz that stands for all
The dark and veined and patterned stone of fame.
ciphers.hint: An opaque quartz, often red, brown, or green.

poem_stanzas:
A time of great rejoicing and of cheer,
A fifty-year and twenty-five and more,
A trumpet and a holiday appear,
A freedom and a feast upon the floor.

A Hebrew year of liberty and rest,
A diamond and a silver crown the year,
A queen has kept two of me, and the best
Of all my days is one of joy and cheer.
ciphers.hint: A special anniversary, especially a fiftieth, or a time of rejoicing.

poem_stanzas:
An evergreen of berry and of spine,
Whose dark and bitter cones give gin its taste,
A shrub that on the hillsides makes its line,
A wood that burns with fragrance and no waste.

A desert and a Bible tree are mine,
A blue and prickly berry is my own,
In gin and game and hillside I define
The sharp and fragrant shrub on land of stone.
ciphers.hint: An evergreen shrub with berries used to flavour gin.

poem_stanzas:
A slender boat of skin or fibreglass,
With paddler sitting low and double blade,
That cuts the waves and lets the waters pass,
A Greenland craft of hunter's ancient trade.

You sit inside and wear a skirt to seal,
A roll can bring you upright when capsized,
An Inuit has named me, and I feel
The northern sea that never quite is prized.
ciphers.hint: A small, narrow canoe paddled by a person, originally Inuit.

poem_stanzas:
A little hawk that hovers in the air,
With pointed wings and tail of barred brown,
That watches for a vole and drops to snare,
And holds its head against the wind of town.

A hunter of the motorway verge am I,
A wind and a great hill may bear my name,
I hover on the wind and watch the sky,
And stoop upon a mouse to make my claim.
ciphers.hint: A small falcon that hovers while hunting.

poem_stanzas:
A land that is a monarch's to command,
A realm of crown and throne and subject folk,
A place a king rules over with a hand,
And every castle has its royal yoke.

A Bible prayer and a game and a book
May bear my name, a fungus and a plant,
I am a bounded realm by hook or crook,
Where subject kneels and king may not recant.
ciphers.hint: A country or territory ruled by a king or queen.

poem_stanzas:
A mounted warrior clad in shining steel,
With sword and shield and plume upon his crest,
Who rides to tourney and to sword and wheel,
And serves a lady and a lord's behest.

A chess piece shaped like horse and rider moves,
A title given now in honour's name,
A champion of the round table proves
My kind, and Galahad has known my fame.
ciphers.hint: An armed and mounted warrior in armour, often in medieval tales.

poem_stanzas:
A criss-cross frame of wood or iron bars,
That lets the roses climb and light come through,
A window and a gate and garden stars,
A patterned screen that hides a view from you.

A crystal grid of atoms bears my name,
A pie of mine is woven on the top,
I am the crossing strips of woven frame,
That screen a window or a garden shop.
ciphers.hint: A framework of crossed strips forming a criss-cross pattern.

poem_stanzas:
A purple field of fragrant spikes in rows,
A shrub that scents the drawer and soothes the brow,
A colour that the evening twilight shows,
A pale and gentle violet in a gown.

A bride is told to wear a sprig of blue,
A French and English garden grows my kind,
A smell of cleanliness and a perfume too,
And sleep and calm are what in me you find.
ciphers.hint: A fragrant purple-flowered shrub, or its pale purple colour.

poem_stanzas:
A narrow shelf that juts from wall or rock,
A place to set a foot or pot or nest,
A sudden step that interrupts the block,
A perch where climbers pause and take their rest.

A window and a climber know my name,
A ridge of ice and rock beneath the sea,
I am the narrow shelf of rocky frame,
That juts from every wall and cliff and tree.
ciphers.hint: A narrow horizontal shelf projecting from a wall or cliff.

poem_stanzas:
A crusty patch of grey and green and gold,
That clings to rock and wall and ancient tree,
A slow and patient thing that grows so old,
It measures air and time for you and me.

A partnership of two lives makes me one,
A pioneer upon the naked stone,
A food for reindeer in the northern sun,
And bearded on the trees of wind and bone.
ciphers.hint: A crusty growth of algae and fungus on rocks and trees.

poem_stanzas:
A cone of fragrant blossoms purple-pale,
A shrub of May that scents the garden air,
A colour that the evening makes a veil,
A shade of violet that the spring will wear.

A Whitman poem mourns a president with me,
A colour and a flower and a wine,
I am the clustered bloom upon the tree,
Whose scent is like a memory and a sign.
ciphers.hint: A shrub with fragrant pale purple flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A tall and stately flower of the field,
A trumpet white or golden on a stem,
A symbol of the pure and of the healed,
A bloom that Easter gives to Bethlehem.

A Bible flower and a boy's name too,
A pad and a river and a colour share it still,
A golden one of Easter is my due,
And gilding takes my name upon the hill.
ciphers.hint: A tall plant with large trumpet-shaped flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A cloth of flax both cool and strong and white,
That sheets and shirts and tablecloths become,
A fabric woven for the day and night,
And ironed smooth and folded, still and dumb.

A closet keeps me in a stack of sheets,
A paper made of rags may share my name,
I am the flaxen cloth where comfort meets,
And beds and tables both my weaving claim.
ciphers.hint: Cloth woven from flax, or household items made from it.

poem_stanzas:
A water flower rising from the mud,
With petals opening on a sacred pool,
A blossom that the eastern faiths call good,
A symbol that the wise and holy school.

A car and an eater and a yoga pose
Are named from me, a pink and holy flower,
I rise unspotted though in mire I rose,
A symbol of the pure and higher power.
ciphers.hint: A water lily sacred in eastern religions.

poem_stanzas:
A stack of sawn and seasoned wood for sale,
A plank and beam and board the sawmill cut,
A timber load that oxen haul and trail,
And build the cabin door and window shut.

To move with heavy feet is called by me,
A room of stored-up junk may bear my name,
I am the timber of the fallen tree,
That builds the house and feeds the winter flame.
ciphers.hint: Timber sawn into boards, or to move heavily.

poem_stanzas:
A tall and spiky flower of the field,
With palmate leaves and blossoms blue and pink,
A legume that a richer soil will yield,
And fix the nitrogen that gardens drink.

A wolf-like name is hidden in my word,
A flower and a beastly thing are kin,
I raise my coloured spikes and am not heard,
And feed the soil that I am rooted in.
ciphers.hint: A plant with tall spikes of pea-like flowers.

poem_stanzas:
The words that singers fit to tune and voice,
A short and singing poem of the heart,
A verse that on a little harp the choice
Of ancient Greece would set to music's art.

A kind of poetry and a kind of voice,
A soprano and a tenor may be mine,
A poem that is made to sing and rejoice,
And in a song the words and music twine.
ciphers.hint: The words of a song, or a short poem expressing feeling.

poem_stanzas:
A large and creamy blossom on a tree,
A southern flower of the early spring,
A bloom of wax and fragrance, fair and free,
That opens before the birds have voice to sing.

A street and a hotel and a film may bear
My name, a tree of the American south,
I flower before my leaves and do not care,
And drop my petals at the summer's mouth.
ciphers.hint: A tree or shrub with large, showy, fragrant flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A loose and flowing cloak about the frame,
A covering that wraps the shoulders round,
A garment worn by shepherd and by dame,
A fold of cloth where warmth and rest are found.

The earth may wear a green one for a coat,
A gas one glows about a lamp at night,
A role assumed is like a heavy note,
And both are called my name, and both are right.
ciphers.hint: A loose sleeveless cloak, or to cover.

poem_stanzas:
A tree with leaves of pointed, hand-like shape,
Whose seeds go whirling down on little wings,
Whose timber makes the violin and the crate,
And in the autumn burns to red and sings.

A leaf of mine is on a nation's flag,
A syrup and a hockey league take my name,
A Canadian will wear me on her tag,
And autumn sets my crown alight with flame.
ciphers.hint: A tree with lobed leaves and winged seeds, whose sap makes syrup.

poem_stanzas:
A stone of polished white and veined with grey,
That sculptors carve and palaces will lay,
A rock that heat and pressure made its way
From limestone into something meant to stay.

A child's small glassy ball can share my name,
A cake of mine is swirled with chocolate,
A sport of gods and ancients knows my fame,
And floors and statues both on me are set.
ciphers.hint: A hard crystalline limestone, or a small glass ball.

poem_stanzas:
A golden flower of the summer bed,
With orange blooms and a pungent, sharp perfume,
A herb whose petals on the salad spread,
And gild the feast with colour and with bloom.

A Mary's gold is hidden in my name,
A day of the dead will honour me with bloom,
I guard the garden with my yellow flame,
And name a colour and a common room.
ciphers.hint: A plant with bright yellow or orange flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A mammal with a pocket for its young,
A kangaroo and a koala and a quoll,
A pouched and southern clan whose babes are clung
And carried till they walk and are not small.

An opossum of America is mine,
A wallaby and a wombat are my kin,
I am the pouched and pouching of the line,
That keeps the infant safe within its skin.
ciphers.hint: A mammal that carries its young in a pouch.

poem_stanzas:
A mixture of a varied kind and hue,
A piece that strings a group of songs in one,
A swimming race with strokes of every crew,
A dish of many things beneath the sun.

A musical assortment is my name,
A salad and a relay share the word,
I gather many into one and claim
A blend of every tune that can be heard.
ciphers.hint: A varied mixture, or a piece made of several songs.

poem_stanzas:
A slender tower beside a temple wall,
With balcony and spiral stair and dome,
From which a voice will summon one and all,
And call the faithful from the street to home.

A muezzin calls from me five times a day,
An Arabic word for a lamp is in my name,
I point to heaven, slender, tall and grey,
And crown the mosque with an ascending aim.
ciphers.hint: A slender tower of a mosque, from which the call to prayer is made.

poem_stanzas:
A solid thing that nature formed alone,
A quartz and a feldspar and a mica flake,
A substance from the earth and from the stone,
That miners dig and jewellers will take.

A vitamin and a water may be mine,
A kingdom and a right and a lick may share,
I am the crystal dug from out the mine,
And gems and ores are all my children fair.
ciphers.hint: A naturally occurring solid substance, such as a rock or ore.

poem_stanzas:
A king or queen who rules a single throne,
A sovereign of a realm by right and crown,
A ruler who must govern all alone,
And bear the weight of every royal gown.

A great and orange butterfly is mine,
A migratory one that flees the cold,
I am the crowned and ruling of the line,
And kings and butterflies my name enfold.
ciphers.hint: A king, queen, or sole ruler, or a butterfly.

poem_stanzas:
A soft and low and continuous sound,
A brook and a crowd and a bee may make,
A quiet voice that scarcely can be found,
A heart may do it for a loved one's sake.

A low complaint of an unhappy crowd,
A heart and a great river both may make it,
I am the undercurrent, never loud,
And village gossip comes and cannot break it.
ciphers.hint: A soft, low, continuous sound, or to speak quietly.

poem_stanzas:
A rounded cap upon a stalk and gills,
That springs up overnight on rotting wood,
A fungus of the meadows and the hills,
A food and a poison, either bad or good.

A fairy ring may circle where I grow,
A colour and a word for growing fast,
I flourish in the dark and am not tame,
And toad and field and forest know my cast.
ciphers.hint: A fungus with a stalk and a cap, often poisonous.

poem_stanzas:
A fragrant evergreen of leaf and berry,
A sacred shrub of Venus and of love,
A wreath that brides have worn and poets carry,
A symbol of the marriage and the dove.

A street and a state and a beach may bear
My name, a Bible tree and a liqueur,
I am the scented shrub that Venus wore,
And poets wreathe me in their flowing hair.
ciphers.hint: An evergreen shrub with fragrant leaves and berries, sacred to Venus.

poem_stanzas:
A sweet and sugary drop within a flower,
That bees and butterflies collect and drink,
A beverage of the Olympian power,
A fruit and a small peach are on the brink.

A juice and a soft drink may bear my name,
A goddess pours me at a heavenly feast,
I am the sweetest blossom's hidden aim,
And gods and bees have found in me their best.
ciphers.hint: The sugary fluid in flowers, or a drink of the gods.

poem_stanzas:
A springtime shrub in pink and white and red,
That blooms in gardens and in woodland shade,
With clustered trumpets opening in the bed,
A bush that for the season is arrayed.

A southern garden shows me in the spring,
A racehorse and a hotel share my name,
I am the showy bush whose trumpets ring,
And woodland paths are coloured by my flame.
ciphers.hint: A spring-flowering shrub with showy, trumpet-shaped blooms.

poem_stanzas:
An herb of green and fragrant, leafy scent,
That crowns a pizza and a pasta plate,
A kitchen garden gives me room and rent,
A pungent leaf that cooks appreciate.

A saint and a great church may share my name,
An herb of Italy and of the East,
I lend my perfume to the kitchen's flame,
And garnish every salad and each feast.
ciphers.hint: A fragrant herb used in cooking, especially in Italian dishes.

poem_stanzas:
A slender tree with paper, peeling rind,
That sheds its silver bark in strips behind;
A grove of me turns gold when autumn calls,
And hangs with catkins before spring's showers fall.

A canoe was once my bark in days of old,
A canoe and a beer may bear my word,
I stand in silver groves and brave the cold,
And scatter seeds where winter winds are stirred.
ciphers.hint: A slender northern tree with pale, peeling bark.

poem_stanzas:
A drooping bloom of azure on a stalk,
That carpets all the woodland in the spring,
A hanging head that bends beside the walk,
And makes the forest floor a blue-green thing.

A flower and a ship and a song may bear
My name, a blue and drooping woodland bell,
I carpet all the forest everywhere,
And by my colour many springs can tell.
ciphers.hint: A blue, bell-shaped woodland flower of spring.

poem_stanzas:
A golden little cup of shining bloom,
That grows in meadows under summer skies,
A flower that will brighten any gloom,
And hold a gleam of sunlight for your eyes.

A field of me is gold in early June,
A farmer counts me as a weed in grass,
A child will pick me by the light of moon,
And hold me under chins to let love pass.
ciphers.hint: A small yellow meadow flower with cup-shaped petals.

poem_stanzas:
A glossy brown that ripens in a burr,
And roasts upon the fire with shells that whirr;
A tree whose springtime candles, white and tall,
Are food for bees and shade for one and all.

A colour and a horse and a tree may bear
My name, and roasted I am sold in town,
I am the nut of autumn, brown and bare,
Whose tree with candles casts a blossom down.
ciphers.hint: An edible glossy brown nut, or the tree that bears it, or a reddish-brown colour.

poem_stanzas:
A small and early bloom of white and gold,
That pushes through the freezing, melting cold;
A cup of purple, yellow centre bright,
The very first to greet the spring with light.

A saffron spice is gathered from my thread,
A colour and a flower and a cup,
I rise before the robin leaves his bed,
And open when the winter gives it up.
ciphers.hint: A small early spring flower, often purple or yellow, whose stigmas yield saffron.

poem_stanzas:
A tall and dark and narrow, pointed tree,
That stands in solemn rows on southern ground;
A solemn shape that graveyards keep with me,
And hills of Italy where I am found.

A poet and a wood may share my name,
A dark and slender evergreen am I,
I mark the dead and keep the solemn frame,
And point a spire into the southern sky.
ciphers.hint: A dark, slender, cone-shaped evergreen tree often planted in cemeteries.

poem_stanzas:
A golden trumpet blooming in the spring,
Beside a lake where nodding heads take wing;
A yellow cup that Wordsworth saw in crowds,
And danced with in the wind beneath the clouds.

A word for yellow and a land of Wales
Are in my name, a trumpet gold and tall;
I bloom before the swallow's song prevails,
And dance in every windy meadow's call.
ciphers.hint: A yellow spring flower with a trumpet-shaped centre.

poem_stanzas:
A little flower of white around a gold,
That grows in every lawn and field and wold;
A child will pluck my petals one by one,
And count the answers till the counting's done.

A name from day's own eye is hidden here,
A flower that turns its face to follow light,
I star the grass when summer days are clear,
And shut my petals at the fall of night.
ciphers.hint: A small white flower with a yellow centre that grows in lawns.

poem_stanzas:
A tall and needle-covered evergreen,
Whose scent is of the winter and the clean;
A cone hangs downward from my somber bough,
A mountain tree of snow and timber now.

A wood for paper and for furniture,
A tree that keeps its needles through the cold;
I stand upon the mountain, tall and sure,
And grow to be a mast in days of old.
ciphers.hint: A tall evergreen tree with needle-like leaves and cones.

poem_stanzas:
A tall and purple spike of hanging bells,
That lines a hedge and woodland where it dwells;
A glove upon a fox, the name implies,
A poison that can heal and can surprise.

Digitalis is my learned, other name,
A medicine for the heart is drawn from me,
I wear a purple spire of dotted flame,
And grow where woodland shade and hedges be.
ciphers.hint: A tall plant with purple bell-shaped flowers, source of a heart medicine.

poem_stanzas:
A creamy, waxy bloom of strong perfume,
A shrub of glossy leaves in southern room;
A flower that brides will wear and gardens show,
A heavy scent that makes the summer slow.

A flower and a scent and a botanist's name
Are mine, a shrub of warm and southern shade;
I bloom in waxy white and put to shame
The perfumes that the summer roses made.
ciphers.hint: A fragrant white or cream flower of a glossy-leaved shrub.

poem_stanzas:
A potted plant with rounded leaves and red,
That flowers on a windowsill instead;
A cranesbill and a bedding plant am I,
With blossoms that will bloom and will not die.

A red and a pink and a white are mine,
A humble flower of the window ledge;
I bloom in almost any soil and shine,
And overflow the balcony's very edge.
ciphers.hint: A garden plant with rounded leaves and clustered red, pink, or white flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A shrub that bears a small and brownish nut,
And catkins hanging like a little lamb;
A wood that fits the hand of one who'll cut
A divining rod to find the water's dam.

A colour of an eye is named from me,
A shrub of catkins and a little nut;
I fill the hedgerow and the coppice be,
And strike from every stump a fresh new cut.
ciphers.hint: A shrub or small tree bearing catkins and edible brown nuts.

poem_stanzas:
A tall and white-flowered plant of poison dread,
Whose spotted stem has many a scholar dead;
A cup of it, in Athens long ago,
Was drunk by one who taught us all to know.

A tree of eastern evergreen and a weed
Are both my name, a poison and a pine;
I killed a thinker who planted wisdom's seed,
And yet a timber fit for bridge and line.
ciphers.hint: A poisonous plant with white flowers, or an evergreen tree of the same name.

poem_stanzas:
A large and showy bloom of tropical red,
With long and jutting stamens at its heart;
A shrub that in a southern summer's bred,
And blossoms where the house and garden part.

An herbal tea of mine is red and tart,
A bloom of island flags and gardens fair;
I open wide a trumpet at my heart,
And show my long and jutting stamens there.
ciphers.hint: A tropical shrub with large, showy, trumpet-shaped flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A spiny, glossy leaf and berry red,
That decorates a Christmas door and hall;
A tree that keeps its green when others shed,
And stands a prickly sentinel in fall.

A name for Christmas and a wood so pale,
A shrub of winter and a girl's own name;
I bear the scarlet berries through the gale,
And deck the hall with every winter's fame.
ciphers.hint: An evergreen shrub with spiny leaves and red berries.

poem_stanzas:
A springtime bulb of blue and white and pink,
Whose clustered bells a heavy fragrance fling;
A garden spike that blooms upon the brink,
And is the herald of the coming spring.

A Greek youth's name is buried in my word,
A gem and a coloured stone may share it too;
I am the scented spike whose bloom is heard,
And every spring the gardens plant me new.
ciphers.hint: A spring-flowering bulb with a dense spike of fragrant bell-shaped flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A rounded shrub of massive bloom and blue,
Whose colour shifts with what the soil will do;
A mop of flowers in the summer's heat,
A garden bush with blossoms large and sweet.

A name from water is inside my word,
A colour-changing shrub of summer days;
I swell in giant balls of pink and blue,
And grow in every garden's shady ways.
ciphers.hint: A shrub with large round clusters of flowers that change colour with the soil.

poem_stanzas:
A brown and leathery ribbon of the sea,
That grows in underwater forests free;
A weed that anchors on the ocean floor,
And shelters many creatures by the shore.

A source of iodine and of a gel,
A food of many a sea-otter's meal;
I am the ocean forest, and I dwell
Where cold and underwater currents feel.
ciphers.hint: A large brown seaweed of cold coastal waters.

poem_stanzas:
A glossy evergreen of ancient fame,
A wreath the victor and the poet wore;
A mountain shrub of Greece, and the same
A crown that praise and glory still adore.

A mountain and a shrub and a crown may share
My name, a green and shiny leaf of praise;
I am the wreath that rests upon the hair
Of winners in the triumphs of old days.
ciphers.hint: An evergreen shrub whose leaves were used to make wreaths of victory.

poem_stanzas:
A plant whose leaves will sting you when you touch,
That grows in waste and rubbish by the wall;
A weed that has a remedy and such
A soup and tea and fibre for us all.

A fabric and a soup are made from me,
A word for being cross comes from my name;
I grow in every waste and by the tree,
And sting the careless hand that comes to tame.
ciphers.hint: A plant with stinging hairs, or to annoy or provoke.

poem_stanzas:
A tall and pink and poisonous shrub of bloom,
That grows in warm and southern gardens bright;
A blossom that can send a man to doom,
And yet a hedge of ornamental light.

A Mediterranean shrub of evergreen,
A flower of the roadside and the wall;
I am both beauty and a poison keen,
And bloom where summer softens into fall.
ciphers.hint: A poisonous evergreen shrub with pink or white flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A flower of many shapes and many lands,
Whose blossoms cling to trees and rocks and earth;
A bloom with lip and spur and waxen hands,
The most diverse of all the flowers' birth.

A vanilla and a lady's slipper share
My name, a bloom of jungle and of glass;
I thrive on tree and rock and everywhere,
And count more kinds than any flower class.
ciphers.hint: A diverse family of showy flowers, including the vanilla plant.

poem_stanzas:
A velvet bloom of purple, gold and white,
With folded petals like a thoughtful face;
A flower of the garden and the light,
That blooms in every cool and gentle place.

A word for thought is hidden in my name,
A relative of violets, small and low;
I smile in winter gardens all the same,
And brave the cold to be the first to show.
ciphers.hint: A small garden flower of the violet family, with velvety petals.

poem_stanzas:
A heavy, many-petalled ball of bloom,
That droops upon a stem in early June;
A garden's largest flower, filling room,
A red and pink and white and fragrant boon.

A name from an old healer may be mine,
A flower of the East and of the yard;
I bloom in great and heavy balls and shine,
And in a hundred petals stand on guard.
ciphers.hint: A large, round, many-petalled garden flower, usually pink or red.

poem_stanzas:
A soft and coloured leaf of any flower,
That falls and scatters when the bloom is done;
A part that curls and drifts with every shower,
And carpets all the garden one by one.

A word for a thin and coloured blade,
The part of blossoms that the bees must find;
I am the piece of which a rose is made,
And when I fall I leave the stem behind.
ciphers.hint: A coloured, leaf-like part of a flower.

poem_stanzas:
A pale and yellow flower of early spring,
That blooms beside a woodland and a lane;
A blossom and a colour and a thing
That promises the warmth to come again.

A name from first and rose is in my word,
A flower that opens when the winter ends;
I am the woodland yellow, and the heard
And hoped-for sign that springtime recommends.
ciphers.hint: A pale yellow spring woodland flower.

poem_stanzas:
An evergreen of needle leaves and blue,
An herb for memory and for the roast;
A shrub of Mediterranean hue,
That scents a garden on the southern coast.

Two names of Mary and of dew are mine,
A sprig for weddings and for memory too;
I am the fragrant, needle-leaved and fine,
And flavour roast and steep in soups for you.
ciphers.hint: A fragrant evergreen herb used in cooking and as a symbol of remembrance.

poem_stanzas:
A grey-green herb of soft and wrinkled leaf,
That seasons stuffing and a butter sauce;
A plant of wisdom and of kitchen brief,
And blooms in spikes of purple on the moss.

A name for wisdom is the same as mine,
A colour grey and green is mine as well;
A bundle of me burns to purify and shine,
And keeps a kitchen's flavour and its smell.
ciphers.hint: A grey-green herb used in cooking, or a wise person.

poem_stanzas:
A giant of the forest, tall and old,
The largest living thing upon the land;
A tree with reddish bark and needles cold,
A tower that has outlived the tallest band.

A Cherokee's name is buried in my word,
A tree of California's fog and sun;
I am the giant tree, the most preferred
By those who measure size and call me one.
ciphers.hint: A huge, long-lived redwood tree of California.

poem_stanzas:
A pointed evergreen of sharpened green,
A tree for Christmas and for paper too;
A timber for a building, straight and clean,
And blue and black and white in varied hue.

A word for neat and trim is also mine,
A tree of northern forest and of cold;
I stand in pointed ranks and hold the line,
And give the Christmas tree its cone of gold.
ciphers.hint: A neat, cone-shaped evergreen tree of northern forests.

poem_stanzas:
A giant flower that follows with the sun,
Upon a stalk that towers in the yard;
A disc of dark with golden petals won,
A plant whose heavy head hangs low and hard.

A name from two things, one a light and one
A flower is mine, a giant and a food;
I turn to face the day until it's done,
And give the world a seed that's oiled and chewed.
ciphers.hint: A tall plant with a large yellow flower that turns to follow the sun.

poem_stanzas:
A tall and mottled tree of patchy bark,
Whose winged seeds go spinning to the ground;
A shade tree standing in a city park,
A maple's cousin, green and broad and round.

A name from fig and mulberry may be
The source of mine, a tree of street and field;
I shed my bark in patches for to see,
And give the summer shade and autumn yield.
ciphers.hint: A large broad-leaved shade tree with mottled bark and winged seeds.

poem_stanzas:
A prickly plant of purple crown and spine,
A symbol of a northern, stubborn land;
A weed that cattle will not touch and dine,
A bloom that guards itself with many a brand.

A nation's emblem and a weed are mine,
A purple tuft on armour of the green;
I am the bonny bloom of Scotland's line,
The prickly guardian of a northern scene.
ciphers.hint: A prickly plant with a purple flower, the national emblem of Scotland.

poem_stanzas:
A cup of colour on a single stem,
That blooms in beds in red and yellow rows;
A blossom from a distant diadem,
A bulb that every Dutchman sows and grows.

A bulb and a mania and a crash are mine,
A cup of Holland in the springtime sun;
I stand in rows and in the market shine,
And once I cost a fortune, every one.
ciphers.hint: A spring bulb with a single cup-shaped flower, often grown in Holland.

poem_stanzas:
A small and purple flower of the shade,
That hides beneath a hedge and in the wood;
A colour and a flower and a maid
Are all my name, and all are understood.

A colour of the rainbow's shortest ray,
A flower of modest mind and hidden worth;
I bloom in secret by the woodland way,
The shyest, sweetest blossom of the earth.
ciphers.hint: A small purple flower, or the colour at the end of the rainbow.

poem_stanzas:
A climbing vine of lavender and blue,
That drapes a porch and pergola in spring;
A cascade hanging from a trellis too,
A fragrant, twining, purple-flowered thing.

A name of an anatomist is mine,
A vine that wrings a tree and climbs a wall;
I hang in heavy clusters from the vine,
And drape a doorway with a purple fall.
ciphers.hint: A climbing vine with drooping clusters of fragrant purple flowers.

poem_stanzas:
A little yellow bird within a cage,
That sings a song for seed and for a perch;
A colour and a bird upon the page,
A singer in a window and a church.

An island and a colour and a bird
Are all my name, a pet of yellow bright;
I warn the miner underground, unheard,
And sing within a cage from morn till night.
ciphers.hint: A small yellow songbird often kept as a pet, or a bright yellow colour.

poem_stanzas:
A giant bird that rides the mountain air,
With wings so wide they cast a moving shade;
A vulture of the Andes, dark and rare,
A soaring shape on every high parade.

A bird of California and of the peak,
A scavenger with naked head and neck;
I am the largest soaring bird, and seek
The heights where only eagles dare to trek.
ciphers.hint: A very large vulture of the Andes and California.

poem_stanzas:
A wild dog of the western plain and hill,
That howls at dusk and hunts a rabbit down;
A trickster of the tales and of the will,
A clever scavenger of field and town.

A Mexican word and a canine are mine,
A cousin of the wolf and of the dog;
I sing at night beneath the moon and pine,
And cross the desert in a lonely fog.
ciphers.hint: A wild North American dog that howls at night.

poem_stanzas:
A large and striped and stinging, buzzing thing,
That builds a paper nest and guards it well;
A cousin of the wasp upon the wing,
A flying, painful insect of the dell.

A basketball team and a car may bear
My name, an insect bigger than a bee;
I sting and buzz and build my nest in air,
And make a paper palace in a tree.
ciphers.hint: A large stinging insect of the wasp family.

poem_stanzas:
A wild dog of the Asian plain and night,
A scavenger that follows after lions;
A howling creature of the moon's own light,
A clever hunter of the dry dominions.

A word for one who serves and toils for another
Is also mine, a dog of Africa's sand;
I cry at night and trail the lion's brother,
And haunt the desert edges of the land.
ciphers.hint: A wild dog of Asia and Africa, or a person who does menial work.

poem_stanzas:
A slender weasel cousin of the pine,
With fluffy tail and sharp and pointed face;
A climber of the trees and of the vine,
A hunter of the forest's hidden place.

A bird and a small animal may share
My name, a furry, quick and climbing beast;
I hunt the squirrel and the woodland hare,
And make of hollow trees a winter feast.
ciphers.hint: A slender, tree-climbing animal related to the weasel, or a swallow-like bird.

poem_stanzas:
A small and damp and four-toed little creature,
That lives in ponds and under stones and logs;
An amphibian with a gentle feature,
And found in ditches, pools and marshy bogs.

A word for a witch's eye and swimming thing
Is mine, a cousin of the frog and toad;
I crawl and paddle on a watery wing,
And cross the garden to my damp abode.
ciphers.hint: A small amphibian that lives in water and damp places.

poem_stanzas:
A spotted cat of jungle and of night,
With tawny coat and stripes and spots and rings;
A climber of the trees in dappled light,
A hunter that on monkey and bird springs.

A name from Mexico is buried in mine,
A cat of South American domain;
I wear a coat of spots and stripes and shine,
And stalk the forest in the drizzled rain.
ciphers.hint: A small spotted wild cat of Central and South America.

poem_stanzas:
A black and white and largest of the dolphins,
A hunter of the seas in packs and pods;
A predator of seals and of the gulf's fins,
A whale that haunts the colder, darker floods.

A name of a kingdom of the dead is mine,
A black and white and toothed and clever whale;
I leap and hunt in family and in line,
And span the seas with fin and fluke and tail.
ciphers.hint: A large black-and-white toothed whale, also called a killer whale.

poem_stanzas:
A hawk that dives and plunges for a fish,
With talons out and wings that fold and sweep;
A fisher of the river and the wish,
A hunter of the shallows and the deep.

A bird that once was named for a river bird,
A fish hawk on a nest of sticks and pine;
I plunge and rise with silver and am heard,
And carry to my young a finny sign.
ciphers.hint: A large fish-eating hawk that plunges into water to catch prey.

poem_stanzas:
A furry creature with a duck-like bill,
That lays an egg and swims in river mud;
A mammal with a spur and a will
To paddle where the currents cool and flood.

An Australian oddity am I,
A puzzle to the scientists of old;
I swim and dive and on the river lie,
And wear a bill and fur against the cold.
ciphers.hint: An egg-laying Australian mammal with a duck-like bill and webbed feet.

poem_stanzas:
A giant snake that crushes in its coils,
That squeezes all the breath from out its spoils;
A serpent of the jungle and the pet,
The largest snake that anyone has met.

A Greek snake and a language and a code
Share my name, a serpent long and strong;
I swallow prey and crush it where it strode,
And coil around the branch the whole day long.
ciphers.hint: A very large non-venomous snake that kills by crushing, or a programming language.

poem_stanzas:
A tiny curled and pink and shelled delight,
That swims in schools and feeds the whale and fish;
A seafood boiled and served with sauce at night,
And served upon a cocktail or a dish.

A little word for a small and weakling man
Is also mine, a crustacean of the sea;
I swim in schools and crown the ocean's plan,
And turn from grey to pink when cooked for tea.
ciphers.hint: A small pink shellfish eaten as seafood, or a term for a small or weak person.

poem_stanzas:
A warty, hopping creature of the damp,
That sits beneath a stone and eats a fly;
A bumpy cousin of the frog and swamp,
A croaker with a golden, bulging eye.

A mushroom and a stool may share my name,
A creature that the witch and garden know;
I hop at night and hide from sun and flame,
And feed on slugs wherever dampness grow.
ciphers.hint: A warty, hopping amphibian related to the frog.

poem_stanzas:
A bald and hunched and scavenging great bird,
That circles on the thermals for the dead;
A cleaner of the plains and of the herd,
That tears the carrion and is fed.

A word for one who preys on others' fall
Is mine, a bird of Africa and Spain;
I wait and watch and answer nature's call,
And strip a carcass clean upon the plain.
ciphers.hint: A large bird of prey that feeds on dead animals.

poem_stanzas:
A bird that hammers on a trunk of tree,
With beak that drills and tongue that pulls a grub;
A drummer of the forest, hear and see,
A resident of hole and wooded hub.

A cartoon bird and a name of a bird
Are mine, a climber on a vertical bark;
I tap and listen for the worm, and heard
My drumming echo through the woodland dark.
ciphers.hint: A bird that drills holes in tree trunks with its beak.

poem_stanzas:
A slender shaft with feathers and a point,
That flies from out a bow and finds a mark;
A sign that points the way, without a joint,
From off a screen or painted on a bark.

A cupid and a signpost use me too,
A straight and pointed thing of wood and flight;
I strike a target and I split in two,
And part the air with all my feathered might.
ciphers.hint: A pointed shaft shot from a bow, or a sign that shows direction.

poem_stanzas:
A wedge of steel upon a wooden haft,
That splits the logs and fells the tallest tree;
A tool for chopping and for clearing craft,
A blade that many a woodsman swings with glee.

A guitar and a word for cutting share
My name, a chopping tool of steel and wood;
I bite the oak and fell it with a glare,
And clear the forest where the saplings stood.
ciphers.hint: A tool with a heavy blade for chopping wood.

poem_stanzas:
A rounded wooden vessel made of staves,
That holds the wine and beer and pickled fish;
A cask that in a cellar's darkness saves,
And holds the goods that merchants often wish.

A gun and a race and a wave may bear
My name, a rounded container of wood;
I hold the rain and roll and store and wear,
And stack in rows wherever goods are stood.
ciphers.hint: A large round wooden container, or the tube of a gun.

poem_stanzas:
A tool that blows a blast of air on fire,
A pair of leather lungs to make it glow;
A thing whose breath can lift the flame yet higher,
And help the blacksmith forge the iron's flow.

A word for puffing and for shouting loud
Is also mine, a blower of the flame;
I breathe into the coals and, with the crowd
Of sparks, I make the forge a living name.
ciphers.hint: A device that blows air to make a fire burn, or to shout loudly.

poem_stanzas:
A long and wooden seat without a back,
Where players sit and judges hold a court;
A place of rest upon the garden's track,
A seat where friends and lovers stop and sport.

A judge's seat and a reserve of players
Are mine, a simple seat of wood or stone;
I stand in parks and courts and at the stairs,
And offer rest to every weary bone.
ciphers.hint: A long seat for several people, or the seat of a judge.

poem_stanzas:
A two-wheeled thing with pedals, chain and frame,
That a rider mounts and balances and steers;
A silent steed that knows no need of flame,
A machine that for a century endears.

A word from two wheels is inside my name,
A cycle that will never need a stall;
I go where legs and lanes and hills can claim,
And lean against a rack beside a wall.
ciphers.hint: A two-wheeled vehicle driven by pedals.

poem_stanzas:
A warm and woven cover for a bed,
Of wool or down to keep the cold away;
A thing that wraps a baby's sleepy head,
And keeps the chill of winter nights at bay.

A word for covering something all around
Is also mine, a layer of snow or cloth;
I cover campers on the frozen ground,
And smother fires and shield the tender moth.
ciphers.hint: A warm bed cover, or to cover something completely.

poem_stanzas:
A narrow-necked container made of glass,
That holds the wine and oil and medicine too;
A vessel that a message can amass
Within, and float across the ocean's blue.

A word for courage and a glass may share
My name, a container of the shelf;
I hold the milk and ink and pickled pear,
And take the shape of what I hold, myself.
ciphers.hint: A glass or plastic container with a narrow neck for liquids.

poem_stanzas:
A little disc that fastens up a coat,
Or makes a machine begin and stop and go;
A thing that has a hole and a small note
Upon the shirt and on the radio.

A badge and a control and a small thing
Are mine, a fastener of the shirt;
I hold the cloth and let the player swing,
And press to start the machine without a hurt.
ciphers.hint: A small disc that fastens clothing, or a control pressed to operate a machine.

poem_stanzas:
A narrow boat that's paddled on a lake,
A birchbark vessel of the native hand;
A craft that leaves a long and silent wake,
And glides across the water to the land.

A word of the Caribbean is mine,
A light and open boat without a keel;
I carry two and paddle down the line,
And ride the river like a spinning wheel.
ciphers.hint: A light, narrow boat moved with a paddle.

poem_stanzas:
A woven floor of wool and silk and pile,
That covers all the boards from wall to wall;
A rug that stretches out and makes a while
Of comfort for the feet of one and all.

A word for covering and a magic ride
Are mine, a floor of woven wool and thread;
I lie beneath the chairs and step and glide,
And make the floor a soft and patterned bed.
ciphers.hint: A heavy woven floor covering, or to cover a floor.

poem_stanzas:
A great and heavy pot for boiling things,
A kettle of the witch and of the hearth;
A vessel where the soup and magic sings,
And bubbles brew upon the kitchen's earth.

A word for a great cooking pot is mine,
A metal vessel huge and black and round;
I hang above the fire and bubble wine,
And hold a feast for all the village found.
ciphers.hint: A large metal pot used for boiling, often over a fire.

poem_stanzas:
A little bed that rocks a baby's sleep,
A frame that sways upon a curved base;
A place where infants softly lie and peep,
And dream with calm upon their little face.

A place of birth and a telephone rest
Are mine, a bed that rocks a child to rest;
I hold the young and nestle at the breast,
And gently sway the darling in my nest.
ciphers.hint: A small rocking bed for a baby, or the place where something begins.

poem_stanzas:
A small and narrow bottle for the pocket,
That holds a drink or laboratories' brew;
A vessel with a stopper and a socket,
A container that a traveler takes too.

A word for a flat bottle is mine,
A vessel small of metal, glass or steel;
I keep a drink or sample safe and fine,
And travel safe within a coat or heel.
ciphers.hint: A small container for liquid, often carried in a pocket.

poem_stanzas:
A jet of water rising in a park,
A structure that a city square adorns;
A spring that plays and sparkles in the dark,
And pours and falls among the garden thorns.

A pen and a source of drink may share
My name, a playing jet of stone and spray;
I rise and fall in gardens everywhere,
And dance with water all the livelong day.
ciphers.hint: An ornamental jet of water, or a source of something.

poem_stanzas:
A hard and rounded cover for the head,
A soldier and a cyclist wear me too;
A guard of metal that deflects the lead,
And keeps the skull from harm in all you do.

A word from a small protective cap is mine,
A thing of steel and strap and visor clear;
I sit upon a rider and a line,
And shield the face from every blow and jeer.
ciphers.hint: A hard protective covering for the head.

poem_stanzas:
A paper shape that dances on a string,
A toy that rises on the wind and dips;
A bird of prey with rapier and wing,
A plaything that a child with joy equips.

A bird and a toy and a cheque may bear
My name, a flying shape of cloth and wood;
I soar above the park on windy air,
And pull the string as tight as any could.
ciphers.hint: A toy flown on a string in the wind, or a bird of prey.

poem_stanzas:
A blade with handle used for cutting things,
That slices bread and carves the roast and fruit;
An edge that cuts and on the table rings,
An everyday and sharp and useful tool to boot.

A word for a surgical blade is mine,
A cutting tool of steel and handle wood;
I sit beside the plate and fork and wine,
And slice whatever cooks and diners would.
ciphers.hint: A cutting tool or weapon with a blade and handle.

poem_stanzas:
A deep and long-handled kitchen spoon,
That lifts the soup and serves it into bowls;
A tool that serves the broth and stew and boon,
And feeds the family and the hungry souls.

A word from a large spoon is mine,
A scoop with handle long for serving soup;
I dip and pour and make the dinner fine,
And lift the broth and from the kettle scoop.
ciphers.hint: A deep, long-handled spoon for serving liquid.

poem_stanzas:
A flame upon a stick to light the night,
A burning brand that guides a walker home;
A portable and glowing thing of light,
A bringer of the fire through the gloam.

A British name for a flashlight is mine,
A beam of light a runner carries high;
I shine into the dark and hold the line,
And light the path beneath a winter sky.
ciphers.hint: A burning brand or a portable electric light held in the hand.

poem_stanzas:
A curved and polished disc of glass or plastic,
That bends the light and magnifies the small;
A part of eye and camera and elastic
And telescope, and helps you see it all.

A word from a lentil is inside my name,
A disc that takes the light and makes it bend;
I bring the distant near and fan the flame
Of sight, and serve the eye and camera's end.
ciphers.hint: A curved piece of glass that bends light, used in eyes and cameras.

poem_stanzas:
A hammer with a head of wood or rubber,
That strikes a chisel and a croquet ball;
A tool that taps and does not dent or blubber
A surface soft, and answers to the call.

A word for a small hammer is mine,
A wooden-headed tool of gentle blow;
I tap the chisel and the peg and line,
And strike the ball and make the croquet go.
ciphers.hint: A hammer with a wooden or rubber head, used for striking without damage.

poem_stanzas:
A cover for the face of cloth or clay,
That hides the features and the wearer's name;
A thing for carnival and for the play,
A false and smiling face of every frame.

A word for hiding something is the same,
A swimmer wears me over eyes and nose;
I guard the welder and the fencer's aim,
And keep the painted player in his pose.
ciphers.hint: A covering for the face, or to conceal something.

poem_stanzas:
A slender, pointed tool for thread and cloth,
That sews the seam and mends the torn-up hem;
A pine and a compass and a clock are both
A thing that points and pierces, small and slim.

A word for taunting someone is the same,
A pine and a syringe and a compass share;
I pierce the cloth and thread and end my aim,
And mend the garment with a deft repair.
ciphers.hint: A thin pointed tool for sewing, or the leaf of a pine, or to provoke.

poem_stanzas:
A thin and flat and white and lined and plain,
A sheet for writing, wrapping, and the press;
A substance from the pulp and wood and grain,
On which we print and draw and make a mess.

A newspaper and a wall and a rock may share
My name, a sheet for writing and for art;
I carry words and news and take a care
To wrap a gift and play the writer's part.
ciphers.hint: A thin material used for writing, printing, or wrapping.

poem_stanzas:
A tall and upright column of the temple,
That holds the roof and stands in rows of stone;
A post of strength and of a symbol simple,
A support that the builders set alone.

A word for a support of society is mine,
A column of the marble and the rock;
I hold the roof and stand in rows and line,
And guard the temple with a steadfast lock.
ciphers.hint: A tall vertical column, or a strong supporter of something.

poem_stanzas:
A jug with handle used for pouring drink,
A vessel with a lip and with a spout;
A player who will throw the ball, I think,
Is also named my word, without a doubt.

A baseball and a jug may share my name,
A container for the water and the ale;
I pour the milk and play the throwing game,
And fill the glass and throw with equal skill.
ciphers.hint: A jug for pouring liquid, or the player who throws the ball in baseball.

poem_stanzas:
A flat and round and shallow dish for food,
A piece of armour for the knight and horse;
A slab of earth that moves and shifts and could
Divide the continents and change their course.

A home and a licence and a number share
My name, a flat and shallow dish of clay;
I hold the meat and armour for the wear,
And bear the food upon the table's way.
ciphers.hint: A flat dish for food, or a flat piece of armour, or a tectonic slab.

poem_stanzas:
A little pouch that's sewn into a coat,
A place to keep a coin and keys and phone;
A hollow in a bag and in a boat,
A hiding place that every child has known.

A word for a small group is also mine,
A billiard opening on the table's side;
I hold the money and the hand and line,
And keep the treasures that a person hide.
ciphers.hint: A small pouch sewn into clothing for carrying things, or a small group.

poem_stanzas:
A small and clasped and leather bag for money,
A thing a woman carries in her hand;
A prize of boxing and a pouch of honey,
A wallet that a lady keeps in command.

A word for drawing tight the lips is mine,
A bag for coins and lipstick and a comb;
A boxer wins me, and a winner shine,
And I go with a lady from her home.
